news.Content: A laptop is a tool you touch all day, just not usually on the screen. Your hands live on the keyboard and trackpad. The display sits upright, a foot or two away, and that setup has barely changed in decades. Apple liked it that way. For years, the company argued that reaching up to poke a laptop screen was a bad idea, even as rivals added touchscreens to Windows machines. • Key criticisms include display wobble, lack of Apple Pencil support, and Mac applications not being optimized for touch input.
• The new touchscreen model is priced $400 higher than comparable non-touch models, with the 14-inch version starting at $2,899.

news.Title: The 'Magnificent 7' stocks are seeing stunning declines
news.Content:
Call it the Unflattering Seven.

Long known as the "Magnificent Seven" stocks, Apple ( AAPL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), Nvidia ( NVDA ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Tesla ( TSLA ), Meta ( META ), and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) shares are acting anything but, especially compared to their 52-week highs.

Meta and Alphabet are effectively in bear markets, down more than 20% from their 52-week highs, as the Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace graphic below shows. Tesla is off by 19.2%, Amazon by 15.1%, and AI chip darling Nvidia by 12.2%.

Meta, Alphabet, Amazon, and Tesla have been crushed following earnings reports that showed pressured free cash flow amid aggressive AI spending. Nvidia is down due to fears that all these hyperscalers are overspending and will be forced to pull back in 2027.

Apple and Microsoft are the only Magnificent Seven names hanging tough, for company-specific reasons.

Microsoft managed to show positive free cash flow this week alongside strong Azure sales growth. Apple isn't being viewed as an AI play, but more as a cash-rich play rolling out new hardware in the iPhone and Mac realms.

"There is too much weakness in tech for the market to ignore," BTIG strategist Jonathan Krinsky said.

Too much weakness in seven of the world's most important stocks for the market to ignore is more like it.

news.Title: LITE's Transceivers Gain From AI Infrastructure Demand: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
Lumentum Holdings Inc. LITE is benefiting from rising demand for high-speed optical transceivers as artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud infrastructure deployments expand. The company's transition toward next-generation 1.6T transceivers, improving manufacturing yields and record cloud shipments position its Systems business for further growth.

Lumentum's Systems revenues reached $356.9 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, up 29.7% sequentially and 122.6% year over year. Cloud transceivers and optical circuit switching were the primary drivers of sequential growth, supported by record cloud transceiver shipments.

Most cloud transceiver shipments remained at 800G speeds, while Lumentum began shipping 1.6T products as planned. Management expects 1.6T adoption to intensify in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and continue throughout 2027. The company is shipping several 1.6T stock-keeping units ahead of major competitors following improvements in product quality and time to market.

Transceiver profitability also improved as manufacturing yields and capacity utilization increased, while the initial rollout of higher-priced 1.6T products supported product mix. Additionally, some initial 1.6T offerings incorporate internally produced continuous-wave (CW) lasers, strengthening vertical integration.

Despite the positive momentum, Lumentum's transceiver business continues to face a profitability gap against leading competitors. Cloud Light, LITE's transceiver business, is generating more than $200 million in quarterly revenues, but gross margins remain below those of top peers.

How Competitors Fare Against Lumentum

Lumentum faces stiff competition from the likes of Applied Optoelectronics AAOI and Coherent COHR in the optical networking market.

Applied Optoelectronics is benefiting from the growing demand for its 400G and 800G products as global organizations are shifting from legacy data centers to AI-driven infrastructures. Applied Optoelectronics has also reduced its reliance on China, sourcing less than 10% of the value of its 800G and 1.6T components from China in the most recent quarter.

Coherent and NVIDIA recently announced a multi-year strategic agreement to develop advanced optical technologies used in AI data centers. As part of the deal, NVIDIA has made a multibillion-dollar purchase commitment for Coherent's laser and optical networking products. In addition, NVIDIA will invest $2 billion in Coherent to support research and development, expand manufacturing capacity and strengthen operations as Coherent increases its U.S.-based production capabilities.

news.Title: SIMO Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Robust Ferri & SSD Sales
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO reported strong third-quarter 2026 results, with both the top and bottom lines surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.35 per American depositary share (ADS) increased 335% year over year and beat the consensus estimate of $3.30 by 31.82%.

Revenues surged 131% year over year to approximately $560 million, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $533 million by 5.07%. Growth was supported by robust demand for SSD controllers and Ferri & Boot Drive solutions, with the latter witnessing a remarkable 2,580-2,585% year-over-year sales increase.

SIMO's Net Income Improves

On a GAAP basis, net income increased to $65.3 million or $1.91 per ADS from $39.1 million or $1.16 per ADS in the year-ago quarter. However, GAAP earnings declined sequentially from $136.1 million or $3.99 per ADS, primarily reflecting a $78 million investment loss compared with a substantial investment gain in the preceding quarter.

Non-GAAP net income climbed to $149.2 million from $33.8 million in the prior-year quarter. Sequentially, adjusted net income improved from $83.1 million, reflecting higher sales volumes and improved operating profitability across the company's storage controller and solutions businesses.

Silicon Motion Technology Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Silicon Motion Technology Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Silicon Motion Technology Corporation Quote

Silicon Motion's Revenues Gain on Storage Demand

Quarterly revenues increased to $560.2 million from $242 million in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, sales improved 24% from $451 million, driven by strong momentum in enterprise and edge SSD controllers, automotive storage solutions and enterprise boot drive products.

SSD controller sales increased 55-60% year over year and 20-25% sequentially, benefiting from expanding demand for edge and enterprise storage applications. Sales of embedded Multi-Media Card and Universal Flash Storage (eMMC+UFS) controllers rose 35-40% year over year but declined 10-15% sequentially.

Ferri & Boot Drive solutions sales increased 75-80% sequentially, supported by rapid adoption of automotive, edge artificial intelligence (AI) and enterprise boot drive solutions. Management highlighted growing contributions from its MonTitan enterprise and AI controllers as the company expands beyond traditional consumer storage markets.

SIMO's Margins Expand Despite Higher Costs

Non-GAAP gross profit increased to $300.7 million from $117.8 million in the year-ago quarter. Gross margin expanded to 53.7% from 48.7%, reflecting improved profitability alongside strong revenue growth. Sequentially, gross margin improved from 50.2%.

Non-GAAP operating expenses increased to $120.7 million from $79.5 million a year ago. GAAP research and development expenses rose to $115.8 million from $69.5 million, reflecting the company's continued investments in storage controller technologies.

Non-GAAP operating income surged to $180 million from $38.3 million in the prior-year quarter. Operating margin expanded to 32.1% from 15.8%, highlighting the benefits of increased scale and a growing contribution from higher-value storage products.

Story Continues

Silicon Motion's Cash Flow and Liquidity

As of Sept. 30, 2026, Silicon Motion had cash and cash equivalents of $845.9 million compared with $74.4 million at the end of June. Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled $953.6 million, reflecting proceeds from the company's convertible senior notes offering.

Operating activities utilized $256.1 million during the quarter, compared with cash generation of $26.9 million in the year-ago period. Capital expenditures totaled $23 million, including $20.1 million for equipment, software, design tools and other routine purchases and $2.9 million for building construction.

SIMO's Capital Initiatives and Dividend Growth

During August 2026, Silicon Motion completed a $1.15 billion offering of 0% convertible senior notes due 2031. The company received approximately $1.13 billion in proceeds and repaid $59.2 million in bank loans during the third quarter.

The board also declared an annual cash dividend of $2.30 per ADS, representing a 15% increase. The dividend will be paid in quarterly installments of 57.5 cents per ADS, with the first payment scheduled for Nov. 19, 2026.

Silicon Motion's Outlook Signals Continued Momentum

For fourth-quarter 2026, management expects revenues between $588 million and $616 million, representing sequential growth of 5-10% and year-over-year growth of 111-121%. Non-GAAP gross margin is projected between 54% and 55%, while non-GAAP operating margin is expected between 36% and 37%.

Management expects continued momentum from enterprise and AI storage applications, supported by its expanding SSD controller portfolio and Ferri product offerings. Despite rising NAND flash prices and pricing pressures in certain consumer markets, the company expects record annual revenues in 2026, representing growth of more than 100% year over year.

news.Title: Fabrinet Grows on the Back of Data-Center Demand: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
Fabrinet FN is benefiting from robust data center demand, with data center interconnect (DCI), high-performance computing (HPC) and new transceiver programs supporting growth. Capacity expansion and emerging optical technologies provide additional opportunities as Fabrinet enters fiscal 2027.

Fabrinet's data center revenues reached $669 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, up 68% year over year and 13% sequentially. The category accounted for 51% of quarterly revenues, becoming the company's largest end market. DCI was the biggest contributor to data center growth, with its annualized revenue run rate exceeding $1 billion. HPC also contributed substantially as next-generation programs ramped up.

Fabrinet is additionally expanding capacity for HPC products and ramping a major customer's next-generation silicon platform. The company expects the momentum to continue into fiscal 2027. A hyperscaler-direct transceiver program is scheduled to ramp in the first quarter, while one merchant transceiver program is expected to start in the December quarter and others in early 2027.

Fabrinet is expanding manufacturing capacity to accommodate rising demand. Building 10 at its Chonburi campus in Thailand is progressing toward completion in early 2027 and is expected to add $3-$3.5 billion in revenue capacity. The company has also commissioned a 200,000-square-foot facility at Nava Nakorn and acquired a manufacturing campus in Santa Clara, CA.

Advanced packaging opportunities in near-package optics (NPO) and co-packaged optics (CPO) could further strengthen its long-term growth prospects. Fabrinet is already building CPO devices for several customers, although volumes have not yet reached scale. Management views NPO as a nearer-term opportunity because it leverages existing capabilities in pluggable modules and advanced packaging.

How Competitors Fare Against FN Stock

Fabrinet faces stiff competition from the likes of Applied Optoelectronics AAOI and Lumentum Holdings LITE in the optical networking market.

Applied Optoelectronics is benefiting from the growing demand for its 400G and 800G products as global organizations are shifting from legacy data centers to AI-driven infrastructures. Applied Optoelectronics has also reduced its reliance on China, sourcing less than 10% of the value of its 800G and 1.6T components from China in the most recent quarter.

Lumentum is a provider of optical and photonic products serving cloud, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), telecommunications, consumer and industrial end markets. Lumentum's cloud and AI exposure is translating into sustained growth, with fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues of $1.01 billion, up 109.3% year over year and 24.5% sequentially.

news.Title: Lumentum stock rises on report of possible merger with Marvell
news.Content:
What happened: Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) stock dropped 12% on Thursday on reports that the AI chipmaker is in advanced talks to purchase optical parts maker Lumentum ( LITE ). Shares of Lumentum surged as much as 5% before trimming gains.

What's behind the move: The potential multibillion-dollar mega deal between the semiconductor designer and Lumentum was first reported by Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter.

An agreement could be announced as soon as next week. Lumentum has a market value of about $83 billion, compared with Marvell's roughly $221 billion.

What else you need to know: The acquisition would give Marvell greater access to optical technologies and manufacturing capacity, which have become critical bottlenecks of the AI infrastructure build-out.

Lumentum makes lasers and other optical components as increasingly powerful AI systems require faster connections. Marvell, which competes with Broadcom ( AVGO ), designs high-speed infrastructure and custom chips that enable AI computers to communicate with one another.

Earlier this year, Marvell stock rallied sharply after AI chip heavyweight Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang described the chip designer as "the next trillion-dollar company.

The company joined the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) index in June. Marvell shares are up more than 190% year to date. Lumentum shares have rallied 140%.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

More specifically, Bloomberg News reported that Marvell was in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum, with deal terms and a final agreement still under discussion. According to the report, a deal could be announced as soon as next week.

"We believe that the actual closing of such a deal would likely take some time to get through both U.S. and Chinese regulatory approval bodies," Stifel analysts said in a note.

On the other hand, Alphabet burned $9.07 billion in free cash flow during Q3 2026, extending a pattern that began in Q2 when it posted its first-ever negative free-cash-flow quarter — and the market is treating any chipmaker tied to Alphabet's infrastructure budget as collateral damage.

Marvell supplies network interface cards, storage controllers and memory controllers that attach directly to Google's custom TPU accelerators, forming the connective tissue of Google's AI infrastructure. An expanded deal also includes a warrant granting Google the right to acquire up to 7% of Marvell's outstanding shares if specified revenue milestones are met — a structure that creates meaningful upside if the Google relationship scales, but introduces dilution risk if the milestone timeline slips.

In layman's terms, when Alphabet's spending power comes into question, that architectural intimacy becomes a liability.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Alphabet's Q3 results showed revenue of $127.6 billion missed the Street consensus of $128.2 billion, while EPS of $2.12 fell sharply short of the $3.02 expectation. Net income dropped to $26.47 billion from $34.98 billion a year earlier.

Google Search revenue grew only 12%, well below the 14.7% analysts had expected, intensifying concern that AI chatbots are beginning to cannibalize the core ad engine that funds Google's entire AI buildout, and, by extension, the spending that flows to chip partners like Marvell.

CEO Sundar Pichai framed the results differently, telling analysts the company is "on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate" and that AI investments are driving the highest year-over-year query growth in five years.

Story Continues

Google Cloud revenue reinforced that point, more than doubling year-on-year to $30.71 billion in the quarter.

Marvell's exposure to this risk is structural. Its most recent quarterly results showed record revenue of $2.74 billion, up 37% year-over-year, with data-center sales representing 79% of the total, a concentration that made the Google relationship a crowning asset when hyperscaler capex was accelerating and now makes it a focal point of concern.

Alphabet's full-year 2026 capex guidance stands at $195–$205 billion, and CFO Anat Ashkenazi flagged further increases in 2027.

The question the market is now pricing in is whether that spending trajectory can be maintained if free cash flow remains deeply negative and Search growth continues to disappoint.

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Lumentum?

For Lumentum, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -1.12%.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Lumentum will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Lumentum would post earnings of $2.99 per share when it actually produced earnings of $3.23, delivering a surprise of +8.03%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. news.Content:

Gross margin increased to 37.3% from 33.2% a year earlier, helped by lower unused-capacity charges and a better product mix.

STMicro forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $4.15 billion at the midpoint, representing sequential growth of 10.5% and a 24.7% increase from a year earlier. It expects gross margin of 39.0%.

news.Title: Earnings Preview: What to Expect From Cisco’s Report
news.Content:
Headquartered in San Jose, California, Cisco Systems, Inc. (CSCO) has built a global business around networking, cybersecurity and communications, keeping businesses connected in an increasingly digital world.

With a market cap of nearly $431.8 billion, the company offers network infrastructure, cloud and wireless technologies, data center solutions, collaboration tools, security software, technical support, and managed services, giving it a broad foothold across the technology landscape.

The extensive reach sets the stage for Cisco's upcoming Q1 FY2027 earnings report, with Wall Street expecting diluted EPS of $1.15, a 42% increase from the year-ago quarter. Cisco has also beaten EPS estimates in each of the past four quarters, setting a strong precedent ahead of its latest results.

The earnings outlook beyond the current quarter looks equally encouraging, with analysts projecting diluted EPS of $4.42 for full-year FY2027, representing year-over-year (YOY) growth of 21.4%. Analysts also expect the bottom line to reach $8.6 for FY2027, marking a 4.8% increase from the previous year.

The market has already taken notice, sending CSCO stock up 51.9% over the past 52 weeks, far ahead of the S&P 500 Index ($SPX), which gained 12.4%. Cisco has carried that momentum into 2026, with shares advancing 43.2% year-to-date (YTD), compared with a 13.1% rise for the broader benchmark.

Cisco's performance looks even more impressive against the technology sector, where the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) has gained 26.5% over the past 52 weeks and advanced 32.7% YTD. Although those returns reflect a strong run for technology stocks, Cisco has comfortably outpaced the sector.

At the heart of that transformation lies Cisco's push into artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, which has breathed new life into its established networking business. The company reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of $17.3 billion, up 17.6% YOY, while hyperscaler AI orders reached $4 billion. These orders lifted FY2026 orders to $9.3 billion, roughly 4.5 times the previous year's total.

Story Continues

Cisco's momentum also extends beyond hyperscalers, broadening its market reach. Networking orders climbed 40%, Silicon One chips secured new design wins, and enterprise and sovereign customers continued upgrading their infrastructure. Looking ahead, management expects hyperscaler AI revenue to reach $7.5 billion in FY2027, nearly double this year's roughly $4 billion.

Wall Street's ratings reflect this improving outlook, with the 27 analysts covering Cisco arriving at an overall "Moderate Buy" rating. 16 analysts recommend a "Strong Buy," one assigns a "Moderate Buy," and 10 rate the stock "Hold."

Price targets provide another measure of Wall Street's expectations, with the average target of $133.08 indicating potential upside of 20.7%. Meanwhile, the Street-High target of $165 points to a possible gain of 49.6% from current levels.

news.Title: Not Nvidia. Not AMD. This Is the Best Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock to Buy in November
news.Content:
The quarterly earnings season is underway, and the initial results from semiconductor bellwethers ASML Holding and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing suggest that the artificial intelligence (AI) boom isn't showing any signs of slowing down.

Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices , two key players in the AI infrastructure space, will report results in November. I won't be surprised to see both semiconductor stocks deliver strong numbers and guidance, driven by the healthy spending on their chips by hyperscalers, governments, enterprises, and AI companies.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

However, I think that there's another key AI infrastructure player that could upstage Nvidia and AMD next month. Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) designs and builds high-speed optical networking components, data center interconnect (DCI) solutions, and optical switches that enable the rapid transport of massive amounts of data in AI data center clusters.

Lumentum will release its fiscal 2027 first-quarter results after the market closes on Nov. 5. Let's look at the reasons why the company can crush Wall Street's expectations and make a parabolic move.

Image source: Getty Images.

Lumentum is benefiting from the next big bottleneck in AI infrastructure

AI chips, such as graphics cards and custom AI processors, are capable of processing huge data sets quickly. However, they need rapid access to all that data to ensure that training and inference workloads can be handled seamlessly. This is why optical networking components are in terrific demand, as the limitations of traditional copper cables don't hold them back.

However, healthy demand for optical networking is creating a significant supply shortage, as production isn't keeping pace. Consulting giant McKinsey estimates that the production of high-speed optical transceivers could fall significantly short of demand through 2029.

For instance, the supply of transceivers capable of transmitting data at 1.6 terabits per second (1.6 Tbps) could be 30% to 40% below demand through 2029. Meanwhile, the demand for 800-Gbps transceivers could be 40% to 60% higher than supply through 2027. The incredible demand for optical networking and the severe supply shortage are driving up prices, significantly boosting Lumentum's margins.

Story Continues

LITE Gross Profit Margin data by YCharts

Not surprisingly, analysts are expecting a 135% year-over-year increase in Lumentum's revenue for the previous quarter to $1.25 billion, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) could jump by 284% to $4.22. Wall Street's expectations are well within Lumentum's fiscal Q1 guidance range. However, Lumentum could spring a positive surprise.

That's because the optical networking market is poised for exponential growth. Goldman Sachs notes that optical networking revenue could jump from $15 billion in 2026 to $154 billion in 2028, a whopping 10x jump in just a couple of years. Lumentum is positioning itself to make the most of this huge opportunity by ramping up production of 1.6T transceivers in 2027.

Lumentum management indicated on the August earnings call that the shift toward 1.6T transceivers could boost its margins. CEO Michael Hurlston pointed out:

Meanwhile, profitability across our transceiver lines continues to improve, driven by gains in both yield and capacity utilization as well as the initial rollout of higher ASP 1.6T transceivers. Our visibility into future cloud transceiver demand is clearer than ever. In fact, we expect the 1.6T transceiver uptake to intensify starting in fiscal Q1 and sustain through calendar 2027.

So, Lumentum's EPS growth could accelerate in the future. The company's adjusted EPS in fiscal 2026 was $8.67. According to the following chart, its bottom line could jump by 5.5x in just three years. However, we have seen that the optical networking market could clock a 10x jump between 2026 and 2028, according to Goldman Sachs.

As such, Lumentum is positioned to deliver a larger increase in earnings per share. That's why investors looking to buy a top growth stock should take a closer look at this name, especially considering that it has pulled back significantly this month.

Now is a great time to buy Lumentum stock

Shares of Lumentum have lost 19% of their value since Oct. 9, when the stock reached a 52-week high. As a result, investors can now buy Lumentum at 43 times forward earnings, which seems like a good deal considering the incredible earnings growth it is poised to deliver.

LITE EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

Assuming Lumentum's EPS jumps to $48.28 in fiscal 2029 and it trades at even 30 times earnings, a discount to the tech-laden Nasdaq Composite index's average earnings multiple of 41, its stock price could soar to $1,448. That implies a potential gain of 58%. However, Lumentum's outstanding earnings growth potential and its ability to outperform Wall Street's expectations could help it command a premium valuation.

So, investors can expect bigger gains from this AI stock once it beats expectations in November, which is why buying Lumentum ahead of its earnings report could be a smart move given its attractive valuation.

news.Title: KLA (KLAC) Q1 2027 Earnings Call Transcript
news.Content:
Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Wed, Oct. 28, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

Vice President of Investor Relations and Market Analytics - Kevin Kessel

Chief Executive Officer - Rick Wallace

Chief Financial Officer - Bren D. Higgins

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator: Thank you for your continued patience. Your meeting will begin shortly. If you need assistance at any time, please press 0 and a member of our team will be happy to help you. Good afternoon. My name is Stephanie, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to the KLA Corporation September Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call and Webcast. All participant lines have been placed in a listen only mode to prevent any background noise. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a question and answer session. Thank you. I will now turn the call over to Kevin Kessel, Vice President of Investor Relations and Market Analytics. Please go ahead.

Kevin Kessel: Welcome to the September 26 quarterly earnings call. Joining me are our CEO, Rick Wallace; and our CFO, Bren D. Higgins. We will discuss today's results as well as our outlook. Which we released after the market closed it is available on our website. Along with supplemental materials. We are presenting today's discussion and metrics on a non GAAP financial basis unless otherwise specified. All full year references we make always refer to calendar years. The earnings material contains a detailed reconciliation of GAAP to non GAAP results. Our comments today are subject to risks and uncertainties. Uncertainties reflected in the disclosure of the risk factors in our SEC filings.

Any forward looking statements, including those we make on the call today, are also subject to those risks. And KLA cannot guarantee those forward looking statements will come through. Our actual results may differ significantly from those projected in our forward looking statements. For any subsequent updates, please refer to KLA's IR website which also contains investor events, presentations, corporate governance information and links to our SEC filings. We will begin the call with Rick providing commentary on the quarter and our overall business environment. Followed by Bren, with financial highlights and our outlook. I will pass the call now to Rick. Rick?

Richard Wallace: Thanks, Kevin. KLA's September quarter beat the midpoint of our guidance ranges, across all key metrics. Revenue was another record at $4.14 billion This, coupled with our December quarter revenue guidance of approximately $4.7 billion demonstrates the growth acceleration we plan for the second half of 26. KLA's performance in the quarter was supported by continued strength in leading edge foundry logic related to AI infrastructure investments, and increasing process control intensity across leading edge devices and advanced packaging. Other highlights for the quarter include KLA delivering operating margins above 46% for the first time ever.

Story Continues

Gross margin was 62.7%, and free cash flow was $1.34 billion Over the course of calendar 2026, the AI demand environment has continued to strengthen as reflected in our performance. Additionally, our strong customer engagement has provided visibility into a more favorable outlook for wafer equipment investment for calendar 2026 and 2027. We see this reflected in our growing backlog and sales funnel forecast. We expect momentum across our business to continue into the December quarter, and we are positioned to deliver significant growth in calendar 2027. We have been proactively working with our strategic supply chain partners over the past year to increase their capacity in order to keep up with our demand.

Advanced packaging remains increasingly critical to AI infrastructure expansion. And advanced packaging roadmaps continue to incorporate more wafer front end process, which drive additional process control requirements, KLA's leading process control portfolio enables the company to address these requirements across a growing range of applications. For calendar 2026, Advanced Packaging Process Control Systems revenue remains on track to hit $1.1 billion or more than 70% year over year growth. Nearly twice the growth rate of the advanced packaging market. The growing complexity of KLA's installed base and lengthening tool life cycles continues to increase demand for services.

KLA services revenue was $850 million in the quarter, up 14% year over year supported by a growing installed base and continued customer focus on tool performance, productivity, and availability in this tight system utilization environment. Finally, KLA's process, PCB, and component inspection businesses are also benefiting from technology transitions and the rigorous performance requirements of high performance computing. In summary, KLA is experiencing strengthening momentum driven by growth across the semiconductor ecosystem. Pace of our backlog growth is a key signal of accelerating momentum and provides confidence in our visibility into calendar 2027. Our September quarter results demonstrate the strength KLA's market position and operating model execution. Semiconductors continue to play an increasingly important role across global industries.

With growth driven by investment in AI infrastructure and expanded demand across a broader range of applications and end markets. Together, these trends are supporting stronger, more durable, and more diversified long term growth for the industry. Additionally, the growing complexity of AI enabled semiconductors is increasing process control intensity throughout the manufacturing flow. Reinforcing KLA's long term growth opportunity. KLA's differentiated portfolio is uniquely positioned to address these requirements. While sustained AI data center investment and broader adoption of advanced packaging architectures continue to expand the company's addressable market. As we look ahead, we remain focused on supporting customer roadmaps, investing in innovation and scaling our global capabilities to meet expected demand growth through calendar 2027.

As we progress toward our 2030 target model, we remain committed to disciplined execution, technology leadership, and our proven capital allocation strategy, which will allow us to create durable shareholder value. With that, I will turn the call over to Bren to discuss the quarter's financial highlights.

Bren D. Higgins: Thank you, Rick. KLA delivered strong sequential and year over year growth in the September quarter. For the first time in our company history, KLA delivered operating margins of over 46%. These results reflect our market leadership and disciplined execution. Supported by our global team's dedication and focus on customer success. Revenue of $4.14 billion was above the midpoint of guidance and rose 13% sequentially and 29% year over year. Non GAAP diluted EPS was $1.22 and GAAP diluted EPS was $1.18 each above the midpoint of the respective guidance ranges. Gross margin was 62.7%, slightly above the midpoint of the guidance range. Operating expenses were $688 million including $395 million in R&D, and $293 million in SG&A.

Operating margin rose 240 basis points sequentially to 46.1%. Net income was 1.6 billion GAAP net income was 1.55 billion Cash flow from operations was 1.53 billion and free cash flow was $1.34 billion The company had 1.31 billion diluted weighted average shares outstanding. For the quarter, a breakdown of revenue by reportable segments and markets, major products, and regions, can be found within the shareholder letter and slides. Moving to the balance sheet. KLA ended the quarter with $4.7 billion in total cash equivalents and marketable securities, and $5.95 billion of debt. The company maintains a flexible and attractive bond maturity profile supported by investment grade ratings from all 3 major rating agencies.

The industry outlook continues to strengthen, with visibility improving as customers increase long term investment plans. Despite these fast pace limitations, customers have been very resourceful and are accelerating delivery expectations across all segments. We are therefore raising our expectation for the wafer equipment market including advanced packaging, to approximately the mid-$150 billion range in calendar 2026. KLA backlog continues to grow, and our sales funnel visibility is unprecedented. Supported by new fab investments by a broad base of customers. We continue to plan for significant growth in calendar 2027.

While we will have more to say about market and customer segment expectations for next year in our earnings call in late January, We currently expect the wafer equipment market to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027. Customer engagement remains robust with numerous new fab projects and greenfield facilities. Scheduled to come online in the quarters ahead. The primary area of focus for our customers is on delivery urgency aligned with new project plans. Against this backdrop, KLA's business momentum and critical role in leading edge process control positions us to deliver accelerating growth for the remainder of calendar 2026 and continuing into 2027.

Our expectations of revenue growth acceleration in the second half of 26 are playing out as more capacity comes online in our long lead time supply chain areas. This is resulting in growth in the second half of calendar year 26 over the first half of approximately 25%. And positions the company for continued sequential growth into calendar 2027. KLA's December quarter guidance is for revenue of $4.7 billion plus or minus $200 million Foundry/logic revenue for semiconductor customers is forecasted to be approximately 60% and memory is expected to be about 40% of semiconductor process control systems revenue to semiconductor customers. Within memory, DRAM is expected to account for approximately 84% with NAND representing the remaining 16%.

As a reminder, these business mix approximations pertain solely to our semiconductor customers and do not fully reflect our total semiconductor process control systems revenue. Gross margin for the December quarter is forecasted to be 62.5% plus or minus 1 percentage point. While the company is demonstrating expected operating leverage across the business as it grows, This is being offset by persistently high memory costs for our system image processing requirements as we have discussed in prior quarters. We are actively engaged across the portfolio to optimize memory efficiency in our systems. Along with other product cost reduction initiatives. These efforts coupled with driving our usual returns based value sharing with our customers, should offset this headwind over time.

Operating expenses are forecasted to be approximately $710 million in the December quarter. We will continue to prioritize next generation product development scaling our business execution and company infrastructure investments to support expected revenue growth over the next several years. And we anticipate these expenses to grow sequentially through 2027 but at a much slower pace than revenue growth and consistent with our business model for operating margin leverage. As a reminder, our business model is designed to deliver 40% to 50% incremental operating margin leverage on revenue growth over the long run. Other model assumptions include other income and net of approximately $25 million expense for December quarter and we expect it to remain at approximately this quarterly level.

Planning tax rate is 14.5%. Our tax rate will vary quarter to quarter due to the geographic distribution of profit and various discrete items. In the December quarter, non GAAP diluted EPS is expected to be $1.44 plus or minus $0.11 and GAAP diluted EPS is expected to be $1.41 plus or minus $0.11 EPS guidance is based on a fully diluted share count of approximately 1.31 billion shares. In conclusion, process control and KLA in particular remain critical to the AI ecosystem build out and benefits from numerous ongoing relevance inflections including increases in leading edge designs across foundry and logic, device size and value, rising complexity and performance requirements, and the growing importance of advanced packaging.

KLA is experiencing strengthening momentum and a broader set of growth drivers across the semiconductor ecosystem. The rate and pace of our backlog growth is a key signal of our accelerating momentum and increased confidence in our visibility leading into calendar 2027. Our September quarter results demonstrate the strength of KLA's market position and operating model execution and support continued confidence in our performance moving forward. These recent results also illustrate the strength of KLA's market leading portfolio, disciplined operating model execution, and continued confidence in improving our performance moving forward. Looking ahead, remain focused on supporting customer roadmaps investing in innovation, and scaling our global capabilities to meet expected demand growth throughout calendar 2027 and beyond.

As we progress towards our 2030 target model, remain committed to disciplined execution, technology leadership our proven capital allocation strategy and creating durable shareholder value. That concludes my prepared remarks. Kevin, please begin the Q and A.

Kevin Kessel: Thank you. At this time, can you please give the instructions? Can you just give the instructions and we will get started?

Operator: Thank you, Kevin. We will now take our first question from Jim Schneider with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

James Schneider: Good afternoon. Thanks for taking my question. Good to see the accelerated growth in the back half Relative to calendar 2027 in your view of $100 billion in WFE, obviously, you have some good things going for you with advanced packaging growth and so on. So can you maybe kind of articulate how you are thinking about the way calendar 2027 shapes up and your level of confidence that you will be able ability to outgrow that 30% rough market number for 2027?

Bren D. Higgins: Jim, thanks for the question. When we look at 2027 and we been saying this for quite some time, as we think the construct for 2027 sets up pretty favorably for us. First, feel very good about our supply situation, right? We have been working at it for the last 12 months. We indicated we see an acceleration in the second half, certain components that have very long lead times. And so getting that to come online was a bit of a challenge in the first half, and we are seeing that play through. And that certainly informs our confidence in the December quarter, but also our views into 2027.

The setup for 2027 around the leading edge, both in terms of the breadth of investment the leading edge, new node investment, we think that sets up very well for the company. Greenfield investment in DRAM, the HBM dynamics and how that is affecting process control intensity, We are also seeing an uplift in process control intensity and conventional memory. Advanced packaging has been a nice growth driver. I do not see any reason why, as we look at next year that part of our business would not continue to grow faster than the market. So we feel overall that the setup is very leading edge centric.

Packaging is augmenting the growth and we think we are well positioned and our supply should be there to be able to enable us to meet the demand. Their demand is strong. I would say that we are I am still behind in supply, but I still I think that the trajectory is good, and we feel pretty confident about the guidance we have given.

James Schneider:

Operator: We will take our next question from Yes.

James Schneider: Sorry. And sorry, just 1 quick follow-up. As you think about the way the shape of 2027 starts to materialize, anything to call out in terms of back half of 2026 was certainly much stronger than the first half. When you look at the CapEx, that was spent on it or is being spent on established nodes, this year as a percent of the total market and you look forward to 2027, could you just maybe describe how that ratio changes? And then I had a follow-up.

Bren D. Higgins: We have seen more investment in 2-nanometer. I mean, look, I think, 2 nanometer and 3-nanometer investments will be the focus in logic. You will see more there. You will also see some investment in the next generation node, so 1.4 So it is different. You did not have any of that, that more advanced investment, and it was more 3-nanometer centric and 26. So I think it sets up I think, good for us constructively in terms of just more 2-nanometer and more leading edge investment in 1.4.

Timm Schulze-Melander: that is clear. And maybe just thank you. And then maybe 1 on memory in 2027. You have discussed your engineering strategy. About how you are going to address that memory kind of impact to your bill of materials. Can you just maybe talk about what you are purchasing strategy is for 2027, from memory, please?

Bren D. Higgins: Well, certainly, our focus early on and through this year has been mostly around securing supply. When things started to ramp in early 26, we felt pretty good about ensuring we had the supply which was no easy feat generally because of the constraints in the overall industry. And as demand has strengthened, we have had to go out and buy more at higher prices. Less concerned about supply. But certainly, we are exposed to the pricing market. And that is informing the commentary that we provided. But I think from a supply point of view, we feel pretty good about the supply we have secured to meet the requirements we have going forward.

Operator: This does conclude our question and answer session. I would like to turn the program back over to Kevin Kessel for any closing remarks.

Kevin Kessel: Yes. Thank you. Thank you, everyone, again for your interest in KLA. We know it is a very busy earnings day, busy earnings so we appreciate it. If we could not get to your questions, hopefully, we can connect here after the call in our callbacks. And with that, turn it back to the operator to formally close-up the call.

Operator: Thank you. This concludes the KLA Corporation's September quarter 26 earnings call and webcast. Please disconnect your line at this time, and have a wonderful day. Goodbye.

news.Title: KLA Corp (KLAC) (Q1 2027) Earnings Call Highlights: Record $4. ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Revenue: Record $4.14 billion, up 13% sequentially and 29% year-over-year; above midpoint of guidance.

December Quarter Revenue Guidance: Approximately $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million.

Gross Margin: 62.7%, slightly above midpoint of guidance range.

December Quarter Gross Margin Guidance: 62.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point.

Operating Margin: 46.1%, up 240 basis points sequentially; first time above 46% in company history.

Operating Expenses: $688 million, including $395 million R&D and $293 million SG&A December quarter guidance approximately $710 million.

Non-GAAP Diluted EPS: $1.22, above midpoint of guidance; December quarter guidance $1.44 plus or minus $0.11.

GAAP Diluted EPS: $1.18, above midpoint of guidance; December quarter guidance $1.41 plus or minus $0.11.

Net Income: $1.60 billion non-GAAP; $1.55 billion GAAP.

Cash Flow from Operations: $1.53 billion.

Free Cash Flow: $1.34 billion.

Services Revenue: $850 million, up 14% year-over-year.

Advanced Packaging Process Control Systems Revenue: On track for approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, more than 70% year-over-year growth.

December Quarter Segment Mix (Semiconductor Process Control Systems to Semiconductor Customers): Foundry logic approximately 60%; memory approximately 40% (DRAM ~84%, NAND ~16% of memory).

Balance Sheet: $4.7 billion in total cash equivalents and marketable securities; $5.95 billion of debt.

Diluted Weighted Average Shares: 1.311 billion for the quarter; December quarter guidance approximately 1.306 billion.

Tax Rate: Planning tax rate of 14.5%.

Other Income and Expense: Net expense of approximately $25 million expected for December quarter.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with MGM.

Is KLAC fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Release Date: October 28, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

KLA Corp ( NASDAQ:KLAC ) reported record revenue of $4.14 billion, up 29% year-over-year, and guided December quarter revenue to approximately $4.7 billion, demonstrating accelerating growth.

Operating margin exceeded 46% for the first time in company history, reflecting strong operating leverage and disciplined execution.

Advanced packaging process control revenue is on track to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, growing over 70% year-over-year, nearly twice the market growth rate.

Services revenue grew 14% year-over-year to $850 million, driven by a growing installed base and increasing demand for tool performance and productivity.

KLA Corp ( NASDAQ:KLAC ) expects to outgrow the wafer equipment market in calendar 2027, with a strong backlog and sales funnel visibility, and anticipates the wafer equipment market to exceed $200 billion in 2027.

Story Continues

Negative Points

Gross margin was 62.7%, slightly above the midpoint, but persistently high memory costs for system image processing continue to pressure margins.

Supply chain constraints, particularly for long lead time optical components, have limited KLA Corp ( NASDAQ:KLAC )'s ability to fully meet demand, with lead times averaging around 12 months and extending for some products.

China revenue as a percentage of total is expected to decline to the low 20th percentile in 2027, growing at a slower rate than the overall business.

Operating expenses are forecasted to grow sequentially through 2027, which could impact operating margin leverage if revenue growth slows.

The company faces potential delays in customer fab readiness, which could affect equipment delivery schedules and revenue recognition.

Q & A Highlights

Q : With WFE expected to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027, how confident are you that KLA can outgrow the roughly 30% market growth, and how does 2027 shape up? A : CEO Rick Wallace said the 2027 setup is "very leading-edge-centric," with breadth of leading-edge node investment, greenfield DRAM, HVM dynamics lifting process control intensity, and advanced packaging growing faster than the market. He noted supply is much improved after 12 months of work, though he is "still behind in supply," with the trajectory nonetheless supporting guidance.

Q : Will 2027 be more linear or back-half loaded, given the strong second-half 2026 ramp? A : CEO Rick Wallace said backlog growth and funnel visibility imply sequential growth for the next several quarters, which suggests a stronger second half, but he expects 2027 to be "more linear" than 2026, without the same significant half-to-half uptick.

Q : Given memory and other cost headwinds, can gross margin return to the 63%+ range in 2027? A : CEO Rick Wallace said the 63%64% target range remains the goal, but advanced packaging and non-semi PC growth are a mix headwind, offset by scale and value-based pricing on new capabilities. He expects improvement as the company moves through 2027, particularly in the middle-to-back half and into 2028, consistent with the March Investor Day model.

Q : When could process control gross margin, which was above 65% in June 2025, return to the mid-60s as DRAM contracts roll off? A : CFO Bren Higgins said on a consistent mix he can see it trending back there in the second half of 2027, since it is difficult to raise prices on existing backlog but new product deals should help. CEO Rick Wallace added that engineering work to use less memory in systems will lower memory content over time, though it takes time to implement.

Q : What are you seeing on lead times, and how are you preparing hiring and the supply chain for a multi-year growth cycle? A : CFO Bren Higgins said lead times average around 12 months, with some products such as Gen4 and Gen5 extending further. KLA is adding headcount in manufacturing, service, applications and engineering, and investing in every factory and with key suppliers, particularly in long lead-time optics, to support a multi-year investment cycle.

Q : Will KLA gain WFE share in 2027 given 12-plus month lead times and low-to-mid-30s market growth? A : CFO Bren Higgins said 2026's first-half weakness was a supply issue rather than demand, and the company remains short on supply today. He feels good about maintaining and growing KLA's relevant share, noting the inflecting parts of the market uniquely benefit process control. CEO Rick Wallace added, "We think we can outgrow next year."

Q : DRAM systems revenue is stepping up sharply in December is this driven by new fabs or rising inspection intensity? A : CEO Rick Wallace said intensity is definitely rising as customers appreciate the incremental value of yield on advanced devices with higher performance requirements. CFO Bren Higgins added that greenfield fabs are driving retooling, yield is "equivalent to printing money," and HBM, I/O counts and logic base die requirements are pushing DRAM intensity in some products toward leading-edge logic levels. Memory is expected to be about 60% of the business in 2027.

Q : How high can WFE grow, and is $300 billion a plausible peak? A : CFO Bren Higgins said the Investor Day view of $220 billion plus or minus $20 billion for 2030 now "looks like a very conservative one," and KLA is more optimistic about higher industry investment levels. The company is having deep conversations with key suppliers about 2029 and 2030 needs to support higher-end scenarios.

Q : Why shouldn't the 2030 model revenue be achievable in 2027 given current WFE levels? A : CFO Bren Higgins said the model assumed service growth tied to installed base expansion, non-semi PC growth, and a few points of semi process control share gain lifting overall share from about 7.5% of wafer equipment in 2025 toward 9%. Those assumptions are not yet met, but he sees no reason the financial model would not perform as laid out as growth comes from the same customers for the same products.

Q : Is the 40%50% incremental operating margin range structurally higher given current performance? A : CFO Bren Higgins said it depends on growth rates: in a normalized environment KLA performs near the midpoint, but with roughly 25% revenue growth it is slightly above the top end, and he expects to be beyond that in 2030. At company growth rates closer to 20%, he would expect performance at the top end of the model or better.

Q : What drove the record CapEx this quarter, and how should we think about CapEx and services growth going forward? A : CFO Bren Higgins said a significant land purchase in India for a new campus drove the quarter. He expects CapEx of roughly 2%3% of revenue, trending to $600$800 million per year as KLA invests at every site. On services, he sees no reason it would not operate at the high end of the long-term growth range in 2027 given installed base growth and high utilization.

Q : Where is KLA in expanding supply, and could December guidance or the $200 billion WFE view have been higher with more supply? A : CFO Bren Higgins said optical components remain the longest lead-time constraint, but KLA does not compete with rivals for its key components, making supply relatively reliable once scheduled. He acknowledged he could have shipped more this year as demand outpaced supply, but incremental supply is coming online month by month. CEO Rick Wallace added that some customers are delaying tool deliveries because their fabs are not ready.

news.Title: 【Hot台股】南亞科漲逾4%後翻黑！網喊「記憶體剩牙科苦撐」分析師示警上檔有壓力
news.Content:
今日社群台股最Hot議題

「牙科優惠時間結束，10點開拉」、「牙科剛綠的是要載人上車？」、「記憶體剩牙科，苦苦支撐」、「昨天沒買到牙科，悶啊」、「牙科重返500大關了嗎」。

「牙科華崩還撐著欸，太扯」、「牙科這波要破前高嗎」、「誰要便宜的牙科？現在大特價給你啊，還不進場看牙」。

針對網友熱議話題…專家這麼說！

HOT台股今日值班專家－啟發投顧分析師白易弘

記憶體大廠南亞科（2408）今（29）日股價震盪，早盤一度衝上497.5元，漲逾4%，距離500元大關僅差2.5元。隨後翻黑又拉回紅盤，不少股民喊「牙科優惠時間結束，10點開拉」，也有股民表示「記憶體剩牙科苦撐」。

白易弘表示，受到昨晚美股科技及記憶體相關族群收高帶動，南亞科今日早盤開高，但由於股價短線已連續上漲，來到480元至500元附近，正好面臨先前高檔套牢區的賣壓，因此開高後漲幅收斂，盤中一度翻黑。

白易弘指出，南亞科近期漲勢較快，短線出現獲利了結賣壓並不意外，若股價拉回至5日均線附近，支撐可能相對較強。他認為，對於尚未進場的投資人，目前不宜急著追高，可先觀察股價是否回落至440元至450元附近，再評估進場時機。

至於網友關注南亞科能否再攻前高，白易弘認為，目前仍有一定壓力，短線須先站穩500元，才有機會進一步挑戰高點。他指出，下周記憶體廠將陸續公布營收，若營運數據提供支撐，南亞科才比較有機會再度挑戰500元關卡。

news.Title: 聯電法說變法會「股價打跌停」 智原連拉2漲停
news.Content:
聯電（2303）28日公布第3季財報，營收創單季歷史次高、晶圓出貨量刷新紀錄，還預告2027年平均售價有望成長約10％，並追加32億美元，要布局先進封裝與矽光子。怎料「法說變法會」29日股價開低走低，股價一度打跌停。另一方面，集團旗下智原（3035）股價延續強勢，連拉2根漲停。

第3季營收742億元

聯電第3季合併營收達742.4億元，季增8％、年增25.6％，創單季歷史次高；毛利率34％，營業利益186.4億元，季增24.7％，歸屬母公司淨利164.3億元，每股純益（EPS）1.32元。第3季晶圓出貨量季增7.3％，突破120萬片12吋約當晶圓，創下歷史新高，產能利用率也從第2季的85％提升至92％，部分12吋晶圓廠產能已滿載，8吋晶圓廠營運亦明顯復甦。

展望第4季，聯電預估晶圓出貨量季增1％至3％，美元計價平均售價維持穩健，毛利率約34％，產能利用率則可望維持在91％至93％。執行長王石指出，高階智慧手機、工業應用需求強勁，車用市場也持續復甦，但電腦市場需求相對疲軟。隨著AI基礎建設持續發展，電源管理晶片（PMIC）、現場可程式化邏輯陣列（FPGA）及連接應用需求可望成長。

明年ASP喊漲1成

聯電看好2027年晶圓代工定價環境改善，預期平均售價將較2026年成長約10％，並從明年第1季開始呈現正向成長。然而，財務長劉啟東坦言，晶圓報價調升不代表毛利率就能同步大幅改善，因為原物料成本也在增加，加上未來數年折舊費用將持續上升，預期2027年折舊費用至少呈低個位數成長，2028年增幅可能進一步擴大。

聯電指出，未來至少3年，折舊與原物料成本都將對毛利率形成壓力，即使平均售價上漲，毛利率仍不容易回到過去景氣高峰水準。這也成為市場評估聯電後續獲利的重要變數，投資人關注漲價效益能否抵銷成本增加，以及產能受限後，營收與獲利還能有多少成長空間。

聯電重挫、智原連2根漲停

儘管營運展望不乏亮點，聯電股價仍遭賣壓襲擊。29日盤中最低殺到跌停價115.5元。相較之下，集團旗下智原受惠明年AI營收可望大幅成長，以及成功接獲美系雲端AI應用之大型專案，採用2奈米GAA製程，股價延續強勢，已連續第2個交易日攻上漲停，來到231.5元。

news.Title: 華東Q4營收看續增  毛利率估穩健
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-29 09:36:14 王怡茹 發佈

記憶體封測廠華東(8110)受惠記憶體封測需求維持高檔，加上價格調漲效益持續發酵，第三季營收22.63億元，季增16.5%、年增20.9%，創2023年以來單季新高。展望第四季，法人表示，隨主要客戶訂單需求持強，加上封測漲價效益持續挹注，預期營收可望續呈季增，明年展望亦樂觀。

華東隸屬華新麗華(1605)集團，營運以記憶體IC封裝及測試為主，為全球主要記憶體封測業者之一，主力產品為利基型DRAM封測，客戶包括南亞科(2408)、華邦電(2344)等。公司近年持續提高集團企業客戶業務比重，其中華邦電為重要客戶，亦為近年營運成長動能之一。

從營收走勢來看，華東今年7月營收6.88億元，8月進一步攀升至7.98億元，創47個月新高，9月營收則為7.77億元、月減2.66%、年增19.11%；第三季合併營收22.63億元，季增16.5%、年增20.9%，創2023年以來單季新高。累計前三季營收61.76億元、年增15.98%。

獲利方面，華東今年上半年毛利率9.57%，較去年同期轉正；營益率2.74%，亦較去年同期轉正，歸屬母公司稅後淨利13.29億元，每股稅後盈餘(EPS)2.59元，上半年獲利已超越去年全年。

法人分析，隨上游記憶體原廠產能維持高檔，後段封測供需持續緊俏，封測協力廠今年初已陸續啟動漲價，幅度約2至3成，帶動華東毛利率明顯改善。隨主要客戶訂單需求維持強勁，加上價格調整效益持續挹注，預期公司第四季營收有機會較第三季成長，毛利率則有望維持10%左右水準。

此外，華邦電日前宣布，將以全現金方式取得英飛凌(Infineon Technologies)旗下NOR Flash及F-RAM相關事業重組後100%股權，交易預計2027年下半年完成。法人認為，隨主要客戶持續擴大記憶體事業布局，中長期有利華東爭取更多封測委外商機。

news.Title: 【股市焦點】南亞科441元貴不貴？新光證券：供給變化成關鍵
news.Content:
記憶體景氣強勢復甦，南亞科(2408-TW)第3季獲利同步衝上高峰，但股價已提前出現修正，市場開始關注這波DRAM漲價行情還能延續多久。

南亞科第3季營收達1,336.49億元，毛利率85.7%、營益率80%，單季每股稅後純益（EPS）25.4元，稅後淨利876.27億元。第3季DRAM ASP季增逾60%，即使位元出貨量季減中個位數，營收仍較第2季成長61.9%，顯示本波獲利主要由價格上漲帶動。公司10月法說也表示，第4季DRAM市場仍處於缺貨狀態，ASP與毛利率仍有續升空間。

新光證券表示，南亞科第3季毛利率達85.7%，反映DRAM平均售價（ASP）大幅上揚、既有產線成本基礎相對低，以及新廠折舊尚未全面進入成本等因素；以股價441元推算，若採5倍峰值獲利本益比，隱含ASP較第3季回落約11%，若採12倍正常化獲利評價，則隱含ASP下跌約52%，顯示市場已開始交易未來景氣正常化的風險。

news.Title: KLA Q1 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in KLA Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

KLA reported record September-quarter revenue of $4.14 billion , up 13% sequentially and 29% year over year, with a company-record 46.1% operating margin and earnings above guidance.

AI infrastructure demand is driving strong growth in leading-edge logic, memory and advanced packaging. KLA expects advanced-packaging process-control revenue to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, up more than 70% year over year.

KLA projected December-quarter revenue of about $4.7 billion and raised its 2026 wafer-equipment market estimate to the mid-$150 billion range, while expecting the market to exceed $200 billion in 2027. China's share of revenue is expected to decline to the low-20% range in 2027.

3 AI Winners, 3 Very Different Paths to Higher Margins

KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC) reported record September-quarter revenue of $4.14 billion, exceeding the midpoint of its guidance range as demand for process-control equipment remained strong across leading-edge foundry, logic, memory and advanced-packaging applications tied to artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

President and Chief Executive Officer Rick Wallace said revenue rose on continued investment in AI-related semiconductor capacity and growing process-control requirements for advanced devices and packaging. The company also projected December-quarter revenue of approximately $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million, signaling an acceleration in growth during the second half of calendar 2026.

→ Comfort Systems Earnings: AI Slowdown or More Growth Ahead?

Bearish Pressure Is Building Around These 3 Stocks

"KLA's performance in the quarter was supported by continued strength in leading-edge foundry logic related to AI infrastructure investments and increasing process control intensity across leading-edge devices and advanced packaging," Wallace said.

September-quarter results

Revenue increased 13% sequentially and 29% year over year to $4.14 billion. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share were $1.22, while GAAP diluted earnings per share were $1.18, both above the midpoint of company guidance.

Gross margin was 62.7%.

Operating margin rose 240 basis points sequentially to a company-record 46.1%.

Non-GAAP operating expenses were $688 million, including $395 million in research and development and $293 million in selling, general and administrative expenses.

Net income was $1.60 billion, while GAAP net income was $1.55 billion.

Cash flow from operations totaled $1.53 billion, and free cash flow was $1.34 billion.

Story Continues

→ A 70% Rally Isn't Chord Energy's Only Selling Point

Analysts Just Raised Price Targets On These 3 Semiconductor Equipment Stocks

KLA ended the quarter with $4.7 billion in cash equivalents and marketable securities and $5.95 billion in debt.

Services revenue reached $850 million, up 14% from a year earlier. Wallace said the increase reflected a larger installed base, more complex systems and customer focus on tool performance, productivity and availability amid high system utilization.

Advanced packaging and AI demand

→ Not All Tech Is Getting Crushed: 5 Names Holding Up Through the AI Sell-Off

The company said advanced packaging is becoming more important to AI infrastructure expansion as packaging roadmaps incorporate more sophisticated wafer-front-end processes. KLA expects revenue from advanced-packaging process-control systems to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, representing growth of more than 70% year over year.

Wallace said that growth rate would be nearly twice the growth rate of the advanced-packaging market. In response to analyst questions, Chief Financial Officer Bren Higgins said KLA expects its packaging business to continue growing faster than the market in 2027, with demand increasingly moving toward higher-sensitivity inspection systems as hybrid bonding and other advanced packaging processes expand.

KLA also expects strong memory-related demand. For the December quarter, foundry and logic are forecast to account for about 60% of Semiconductor Process Control Systems revenue from semiconductor customers, while memory is expected to account for approximately 40%. Within memory, DRAM is expected to represent about 84% and NAND about 16%.

Wallace said process-control intensity is rising in DRAM as customers seek higher yields and meet more stringent performance expectations, particularly for advanced memory products. Higgins added that some DRAM products now have process-control intensity comparable with leading-edge logic, aided by greenfield fab investment and demand for high-bandwidth memory.

Industry outlook and capacity investments

KLA raised its estimate for the calendar 2026 wafer-equipment market, including advanced packaging, to approximately the mid-$150 billion range. Higgins said customers are increasing long-term investment plans despite fab-space limitations and that KLA's sales funnel visibility is "unprecedented," supported by new fab investments from a broad customer base.

For calendar 2027, the company expects the wafer-equipment market to exceed $200 billion. Higgins said KLA anticipates sequential revenue growth over the next several quarters, with a more linear progression than the sharp second-half increase anticipated in 2026.

The company said it has been working with supply-chain partners for the past year to expand capacity, particularly for long-lead-time components such as optics. Higgins said average lead times are about 12 months, with some Gen4 and Gen5 product lines taking longer.

KLA is investing in manufacturing, service, engineering and applications staffing, as well as factory capacity. Higgins said capital expenditures should trend higher over the next several years, estimating annual spending of roughly $600 million to $800 million. He noted that a significant land purchase in India for a new campus was a major contributor to the quarter's capital spending.

Management said supply availability had constrained shipments during the first half of 2026, but incremental capacity is now coming online. Wallace also noted that customers can face their own constraints, including delays in clean-room construction, materials and power availability.

Margins, China and December outlook

KLA forecast December-quarter gross margin of 62.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point, and operating expenses of approximately $710 million. Higgins said persistently elevated memory costs for system image-processing requirements remain a margin headwind, though the company is working to reduce memory usage in its systems, lower product costs and capture value-based pricing on new capabilities.

For the December quarter, KLA expects non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.44, plus or minus $0.11, and GAAP diluted EPS of $1.41, plus or minus $0.11. The company's forecast assumes approximately 1.306 billion fully diluted shares, other expense of about $25 million and a planning tax rate of 14.5%.

On China, Higgins said the country's revenue contribution is expected to decline as a percentage of total sales despite modest growth in absolute terms. He expects China to represent roughly 27% to 29% of revenue in the fourth quarter and to fall to the low-20% range in calendar 2027, as wafer-equipment spending outside China grows more rapidly.

About KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC)

KLA Corporation (NASDAQ: KLAC) develops process control, inspection and yield management solutions for the semiconductor and other advanced manufacturing industries. Its technologies help manufacturers identify defects, measure critical dimensions and monitor production processes to improve quality, reliability and manufacturing efficiency.

The company's product portfolio includes wafer and reticle inspection systems, metrology and measurement tools, defect review and classification systems, and software for analyzing manufacturing data.

news.Title: 2 Millionaire-Maker Custom Silicon Stocks Powering the AI Infrastructure Supercycle
news.Content:
Graphics processing units (GPUs) are the core hardware that is used to train advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models, but they're not the only semiconductors that are useful when it comes to AI. Application specific integrated circuits (ASICs) are chips that are custom designed to excel at specific tasks.

ASICs aren't as versatile or generally powerful as GPUs, but they can actually be significantly more powerful and efficient when it comes to handling the tasks they were designed for. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) are two leading players in the custom silicon space that have delivered huge wins for investors thanks in part to their wins with ASICs.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

1. Broadcom

In addition to providing networking hardware and software services, Broadcom has emerged as a leading provider of custom ASIC designs.

The company has partnered with Alphabet to produce the software giant's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs).

In addition to Alphabet, Broadcom also counts Meta Platforms , OpenAI, and Anthropic among its ASIC customers.

It's been scoring huge sales and earnings growth in conjunction with rising demand for its custom chips and AI-related networking solutions.

In this year's third quarter, Broadcom's artificial intelligence semiconductor revenue rose 221% year over year to $16.7 billion, largely driven by demand for its custom AI accelerator chips and AI networking solutions. Meanwhile, net income rose roughly 216% to hit roughly $13.1 billion. For the fourth quarter, the company said that it expected AI revenue to increase 236% annually to reach $21.7 billion.

Over the last 15 years, Broadcom has delivered a dividend-adjusted total return of roughly 13,470%. That means that if you invested $25,000 in the stock a decade ago and held on to your position, it would now be worth roughly $3.4 million.

AVGO PS Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

Broadcom has actually seen some substantial valuation pullbacks in conjunction with concerns about valuations across the broader AI industry, but it still trades at roughly 28 times this year's expected earnings and 15 times expected sales. While the company still has a growth-dependent valuation, it has a very strong net income margin profile and has been growing revenue at an impressive clip that could support valuation gains.

Story Continues

2. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, or TSMC as it's often called, doesn't design ASICs or any other kind of semiconductor. Instead, the company manufactures its customers' chip designs -- and it absolutely dominates the chip manufacturing space.

When it comes to high-end ASICs from Broadcom, Marvell Technology , and other designers, TSMC is the go-to choice for chip fabrication. This means that TSMC stands out as a strong pick-and-shovel play for benefiting from the growth of the custom semiconductor market, as well as the growth of the broader chip industry.

According to many estimates, TSMC controls over 90% of the market for high-end semiconductors designed for artificial intelligence and other high-performance computing applications. The company's status as the leading global provider of advanced AI chips has translated into stellar stock performance.

TSMC stock has delivered a total return of roughly 4,720% over the last 15 years. If you had invested $25,000 in the stock 15 years ago, your holdings would now be worth roughly $1.2 million.

TSM PS Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

As with Broadcom, TSMC has seen some recent valuation volatility connected to concerns that an AI valuation bubble could be on the verge of bursting. On the other hand, the business retains a dominant position in the chip fabrication that is crucial to global technology supply chains -- and strong demand trends and margins could help the stock go on to reach new highs.

news.Title: Marvell nears deal for optical supplier Lumentum to bolster hardware, report says
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Shares of Lumentum Holdings Inc (NASDAQ:LITE) surged more than 6% in premarket trading Thursday after Bloomberg reported that chipmaker Marvell Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MRVL) is in advanced discussions to acquire the optical equipment supplier. Meanwhile, Marvell stock tumbled over 12%, weighed down by the prospect of digesting a megadeal alongside broader sector pressure stemming from Alphabet Inc.'s steep cash-flow burn.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

A transaction could be finalized as soon as next week, according to Bloomberg, though discussions remain private and terms could still shift. An outright purchase of Lumentum, valued at approximately $83 billion against Marvell's $221 billion market capitalization, would rank among the ten largest tech and telecom mergers in history, according to Bloomberg data.

The industrial rationale centers on the intensifying race to eliminate data bottlenecks in artificial intelligence clusters. Lumentum produces indium phosphide (InP) lasers and optical components that move massive volumes of data at high speeds, an architecture increasingly displacing legacy copper connections as facilities pack together denser computing nodes.

Demand for these high-speed optical connections has already overwhelmed available industry supply. Lumentum Chief Executive Officer Michael Hurlston stated this month that the company's optical components are sold out through early 2029, Bloomberg noted, leaving it unable to meet an estimated 70% of demand for certain products next year despite aggressive expansions, such as a planned $350 million investment in Japan.

For Marvell, absorbing Lumentum would resolve immediate component shortages while vertically integrating its connectivity portfolio. Building on its prior acquisition of photonic startup Celestial AI, Marvell would pair its industry-leading digital signal processors (DSPs) with Lumentum's laser fabrication, directly challenging peers like Broadcom Inc (NASDAQ:AVGO) in full system-level modules.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg highlighted this strategic codesign in a client note, arguing that controlling both silicon and optics allows the company to architect networking hardware across scale-out, scale-across, and co-packaged optics (CPO) architectures. Svanberg noted that "the ability to codesign silicon and optics around system-level performance, power, and latency could be a significant competitive differentiator for a combined Marvell-Lumentum, as few suppliers would span switching, XPU Attach, DSPs, analog, silicon photonics, and InP lasers under one roof."

Story Continues

Svanberg also pointed out that the transaction could serve as a hedge against geopolitical crosswinds, positioning Marvell as a domestic powerhouse if U.S. restrictions materialize against Chinese optical transceiver vendors that currently supply an estimated 70% of the market. However, Svanberg cautioned that actual closing "would likely take some time to get through both U.S. and Chinese regulatory approval bodies," while risking friction with merchant DSP customers who might turn to rival silicon suppliers.

Wall Street sentiment diverged sharply regarding transaction structure and financial feasibility. Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh reiterated an Outperform rating and $1,140 price target on Lumentum, calculating that historical semiconductor buyouts commanded an average 38% premium that could imply an offer price topping $1,260 per share given Lumentum's commanding moat in optical switching and lasers.

By contrast, Raymond James analyst Simon Leopold expressed skepticism over the scale of the commitment, reiterating a Strong Buy on Marvell with a $295 price target while questioning the balance sheet mechanics. Noting Marvell's roughly $4 billion in cash against $5 billion in long-term debt, Leopold cautioned that "scenarios suggest a combination could be EPS neutral by CY28 or dilute Marvell's EPS by +10% depending on the size and structure, which casts some doubt on the likelihood."

Compounding Marvell's stock decline, Alphabet's third-quarter earnings report revealed a $9.07 billion free-cash-flow burn, sparking sector-wide anxiety among custom silicon suppliers. Marvell manufactures storage controllers and network interface cards tailored to Google's Tensor Processing Units, leaving its near-term trading tied directly to hyperscaler infrastructure budgets.

Loans grew to $11.9 billion, with commercial and consumer lending driving gains, while fee-based businesses also reached record revenue levels. The company raised its quarterly dividend 8.1% year over year to $0.40 per share.

NBT Bancorp (NASDAQ:NBTB) reported record third-quarter earnings as loan growth, a higher net interest margin and fee-based business contributions lifted results. The company posted net income of $58 million, or $1.11 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026.

President and CEO Scott Kingsley said the company generated stronger earnings than in both the prior-year quarter and the second quarter of 2026. Operating return on assets was 1.41%, while operating return on tangible equity was 16.53%. Tangible book value per share reached $27.75, up 8.8% from a year earlier.

NBT raised its quarterly dividend to $0.40 per share, an 8.1% increase from the prior year. Kingsley said capital deployment priorities remain centered on supporting organic growth and maintaining annual dividend increases, while the company also evaluates strategic opportunities and measured share repurchases.

Record Net Interest Income and Loan Growth

Chief Financial Officer Annette Burns said net interest income rose to a record $143 million, increasing $5 million from the second quarter and more than 5% from the third quarter of 2025. Net interest margin expanded five basis points sequentially to 3.78%.
