news.Title: Investors Heavily Search Texas Instruments Incorporated (TXN): Here is What You Need to Know
news.Content:
Texas Instruments (TXN) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.

Shares of this chipmaker have returned +7.1% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -0.8% change. The Zacks Semiconductor - General industry, to which Texas Instruments belongs, has lost 5.9% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Texas Instruments is expected to post earnings of $2.53 per share, indicating a change of +99.2% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +19.6% over the last 30 days.

The consensus earnings estimate of $8.85 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +62.4%. This estimate has changed +5.1% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $11.03 indicates a change of +24.7% from what Texas Instruments is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +12.1%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) for Texas Instruments.

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Revenue Growth Forecast

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

In the case of Texas Instruments, the consensus sales estimate of $6.09 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +37.7%. The $22.26 billion and $25.62 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +25.9% and +15.1%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Texas Instruments reported revenues of $6.06 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +27.7%. EPS of $2.62 for the same period compares with $1.48 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.93 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +2.17%. The EPS surprise was +9.17%.

Over the last four quarters, Texas Instruments surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates three times over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Texas Instruments is graded F on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Conclusion

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Texas Instruments. However, its Zacks Rank #1 does suggest that it may outperform the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: Here's How Much a $1000 Investment in Texas Instruments Made 10 Years Ago Would Be Worth Today
news.Content:
How much a stock's price changes over time is important for most investors, since price performance can both impact your investment portfolio and help you compare investment results across sectors and industries.

The fear of missing out, or FOMO, also plays a factor in investing, especially with particular tech giants, as well as popular consumer-facing stocks.

What if you'd invested in Texas Instruments (TXN) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to TXN for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?

Texas Instruments' Business In-Depth

With that in mind, let's take a look at Texas Instruments' main business drivers.

Headquartered in Dallas, TX, Texas Instruments Incorporated is an original equipment manufacturer of analog, mixed-signal and digital signal processing (DSP) integrated circuits.

Texas Instruments has manufacturing and design facilities, including wafer fabrication and assembly/test operations in North America, Asia and Europe.

Management's strategy has been to build assets that would be fully utilized through their lifetimes and outsource any excess demand in peak situations to outside foundries.

In 2025, Texas Instruments generated total revenues of $17.68 billion, up 13% from 2024. The company has two reporting financial segments, Analog and Embedded Processing. It reports the results of its remaining business activities in Other.

Analog segment revenues grew 15% to $14.01 billion and accounted for approximately 79% of total revenues in 2025. Analog products have been categorized into two categories, Power and Signal Chain. Power products manage and distribute electricity, while Signal Chain products sense, condition and convert real-world signals.

Revenues from the Embedded Processing segment rose 6% to $2.70 billion and contributed approximately 15% to 2025 total revenues. This segment includes microcontrollers, processors, wireless connectivity and radar products.

The Other business generated $979 million in revenues and accounted for approximately 6% of 2025 total sales. The segment includes smaller product lines, such as DLP products, calculators and certain application-specific integrated circuits. Revenues from this segment increased 3% in 2025.

The company's products are sold in industrial, personal electronics, automotive, data center and communications equipment markets. In 2025, industrial and automotive each represented 33% of revenue. Personal electronics accounted for 21%, data center 9% and communications equipment 3%. Calculators represented about 1% of revenue.

Texas Instruments has more than 80,000 products and over 100,000 customers. In 2025, more than 80% of revenue was generated through direct sales channels.

Story Continues

Bottom Line

Anyone can invest, but building a successful investment portfolio requires research, patience, and a little bit of risk. So, if you had invested in Texas Instruments, ten years ago, you're likely feeling pretty good about your investment today.

According to our calculations, a $1000 investment made in October 2016 would be worth $4,157.30, or a gain of 315.73%, as of October 27, 2026, and this return excludes dividends but includes price increases.

Compare this to the S&P 500's rally of 258.82% and gold's return of 203.96% over the same time frame.

Analysts are anticipating more upside for TXN.

Texas Instruments is benefiting from a broad recovery in industrial and automotive demand and sustained data center expansion. Its analog and embedded portfolios serve diverse, long-lived applications. Internal manufacturing and growing capacity strengthen supply reliability while supporting margin recovery as utilization rises. Rising cash generation provides greater room for dividends and long-term investment. The planned Silicon Labs acquisition could extend its wireless connectivity reach. Management's outlook points to continued demand across its core markets. Semiconductor cyclicality, pricing competition, trade exposure and debt remain risks. Equipment delivery constraints could also slow capacity additions. Nonetheless, improving factory economics and a wider range of growth opportunities support an Outperform view.

The stock is up 7.12% over the past four weeks, and no earnings estimate has gone lower in the past two months, compared to 9 higher, for fiscal 2026. The consensus estimate has moved up as well.

news.Title: Broadcom vs. Taiwan Semiconductor: Two AI Powerhouses, One Surprising Revenue Trend
news.Content:
The global artificial intelligence boom has created enormous opportunities for semiconductor companies, and few are better positioned to capitalize on that demand than Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM).

Both companies play critical roles in powering modern data centers and AI infrastructure, but they operate at different stages of the semiconductor supply chain. Broadcom designs advanced chips and networking technology, while Taiwan Semiconductor manufactures the chips that power many of the world's leading technology companies.

As investment in AI infrastructure accelerates, both companies have experienced impressive revenue growth. However, their quarterly results reveal an interesting distinction in how each is capturing that demand. For investors, the question isn't simply which company generates more revenue, but which can sustain its growth as the AI industry continues to expand.

Broadcom vs. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Revenue over the last 8 quarters. Figures: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing shown in U.S. dollars, converted from New Taiwan dollars.

Broadcom: An Accelerating Upward Revenue Trajectory

Broadcom operates as a global technology company specializing in advanced semiconductors, networking equipment, and enterprise software. Its products play an increasingly important role in AI data centers, where growing demand for computing power is driving substantial revenue growth.

That demand was evident in Broadcom's latest earnings report. In September 2026, the company reported quarterly revenue of $29.6 billion, an 86% increase from the prior year. AI semiconductor revenue was particularly impressive, climbing 221% to $16.7 billion as major technology companies continued investing heavily in custom AI chips and networking infrastructure. Management expects that momentum to continue, projecting approximately $21.7 billion in AI semiconductor revenue for the following quarter.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing: Consistent Revenue Expansion

Taiwan Semiconductor operates the world's largest contract semiconductor manufacturing business, producing advanced chips for technology giants like Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), and even Broadcom. Its manufacturing capabilities are critical to the global AI infrastructure buildout, with growing demand for computing power driving substantial revenue growth.

That demand was evident in the company's latest earnings report. In October 2026, Taiwan Semiconductor reported record quarterly revenue of $46.7 billion, an increase of more than 41% from the prior year. In addition, its newest two-nanometer chips represented a growing share of production. With demand showing little sign of slowing, management expects fourth-quarter revenue to range from $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, potentially extending the company's impressive growth streak.

Foolish Take

The revenue trends of Broadcom and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing tell an interesting story. Both companies are clearly benefiting from the global AI infrastructure boom, but one is growing considerably faster despite generating less revenue overall.

Taiwan Semiconductor remains the larger business, with quarterly revenue climbing from roughly $26 billion in late 2024 to nearly $40 billion by the second quarter of 2026. Revenue then reached approximately $47 billion in the third quarter, reflecting continued demand for the advanced chips powering today's AI systems.

Broadcom's growth, however, is particularly striking. Quarterly revenue more than doubled over the same period, rising from approximately $14 billion to $29 billion. That's considerably faster than Taiwan Semiconductor's roughly 50% increase.

The difference between these two comes down to how each company benefits from the growing demand for AI infrastructure. Taiwan Semiconductor manufactures advanced chips for a broad range of customers, while Broadcom designs specialized processors and networking equipment that help power increasingly complex AI systems.

Both companies have substantial opportunities ahead, but Broadcom's accelerating revenue growth is noteworthy. While Taiwan Semiconductor remains the larger business, Broadcom has demonstrated an impressive ability to capitalize on the AI boom.

news.Title: 智原Q4營收估季持平；明年三大產品線齊向上
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-27 16:42:18 黃立安 發佈

ASIC設計服務暨矽智財(IP)廠智原(3035)今(27)日舉行法說會，總經理王國雍表示，今(2026)年第四季IP業績可望續創高，NRE業務也將顯著成長，不過量產業務可能下滑，整體單季營收將較第三季的36.6億元約略持平，毛利率則回升至45%。2027年營收將成長兩位數，包括IP、NRE和量產三大產品線均可望同步向上。此外，近期先進製程成功接下美國客戶2奈米雲端AI應用專案，總金額高達數千萬美元，成為智原史上最大規模專案。

針對該2奈米專案，王國雍表示，此為首個2奈米環繞閘極(GAA)製程專案，原本客戶計劃採用4奈米製程，但考量到產品生命週期，決定改採2奈米製程，且專案總金額達數千萬美元，預計2027年上半年將有第一筆收入入帳，後續依進度認列，此案是智原史上最大金額的專案，將採用三星的晶圓代工，另外還與聯電(2303)及記憶體廠等夥伴合作。

王國雍指出，此項AI專案對公司深具指標性意義，並於四個面向均創下公司紀錄-設計製程、設計複雜度、NRE金額規模及高階封裝技術，同時此除證明客戶對公司設計能力的肯定及信賴，亦為後續先進製程及高階封裝接單及推廣建立了重要的指標性案例。

回顧第三季表現，智原在量產業務帶動下，單季營收達36.6億元，不僅優於原先預期，更逆勢季增11%、年增13%；毛利率42.5%，季減2.7個百分點、年增9.3個百分點；營業利益為2.1億元，季減21%，雖較第二季小幅回落，但受到營收規模擴大及毛利結構改善，年增達443%；營業利益率5.8%；稅後淨利2.8億元，季增41%，年增84%，EPS為1.07元。

智原2026年第三季營運創下多項紀錄，包括IP營收創歷史新高，量產及單季合併營收雙雙寫下歷年同期新高。

以產品別來看，IP營收4.5億元，季增4%，年增8%，創下歷史新高；NRE收入為3.1億元，季減31%，年減37%；量產營收則為第三季季主要成長動能，不僅MCU相關營收再創單季新高，ASIC量產在AI相關高階封裝專案出貨動能加速下，亦同步走揚，推升量產營收季增20%，年增25%，達29.1億元，創下歷年同期高點。

news.Title: 智原第三季每股賺1.07元，成功搶下2奈米AI專案明年上半年開始入帳
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者李純君報導】智原(3035)今日召開法說會，公布第三季成績單，單季本業部分，量產業務大增，業外收益也同時進補，帶動單季每股淨利1.07元，展望第四季，估營收與前季持平，IP持續成長創新高，NRE顯著成長，量產業務下滑，至於第四季毛利率估為45%。產線斬獲部分，獲得國際客戶開案，採用2奈米GAA製程，承接瞄準雲端AI應用之大型專案，預計2027年上半年會開始有收益。智原第三季受惠量產業務大幅成長，單季合併營收達36.64億元，季增10.6%、年增13.2%；營收中，IP營收4.48億元，季增3.5%、年增8.4%；NRE營收3.09億元，季減31.3%、年減37.1%；量產業務營收則達29.07億元，季增19.6%、年增24.7%，成為推升整體營收成長的主要動能。

獲利方面，智原第三季營業毛利15.57億元，季增3.9%、年增44.9%；毛利率42.5%，雖低於第二季的45.2%，但仍明顯高於去年同期的33.2%。第三季營業利益率為5.8%，低於第二季的8.2%，但優於去年同期的1.3%。但智原第三季業外收入達到2.66億元，季增138.8%、年增53.2%，主因業外轉投資評價利益挹注，挹注第三季本期淨利增至3.69億元，季增29.2%、年增124.1%。第三季歸屬母公司業主稅後淨利為2.79億元，季增40.8%、年增83.8%，單季每股淨利1.07元，。

展望第四季，公司自估，營收與第三季相比，大致約持平，毛利率估為45%。產線方面，IP持續成長創新高，NRE顯著成長，量產業務下滑。至於在產品線的斬獲部分，智原總經理王國雍透露，藉由和聯電(2303)、三星，以及記憶體廠等廠商的合作，公司已經獲得總金額數千萬美元、美系業者的2奈米AI雲端專案訂單。而整體2027年，智原看法樂觀，營收會年增雙位數百分比，三大產線都會年增。

news.Title: 智原攜手三星、聯電　搶下美國2奈米雲端AI專案訂單
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中新竹2026年10月27日電）特殊應用晶片廠智原 (3035) 總經理王國雍今天表示，透過與三星（Samsung）、聯電 (2303) 和記憶體廠等夥伴合作，成功搶下美國廠商2奈米雲端人工智慧（AI）專案訂單，總金額高達數千萬美元，是智原史上最大規模專案。

智原今天召開線上法人說明會，王國雍說，智原客戶委託設計（NRE）業務在先進製程有新斬獲，成功搶下2奈米環繞閘極（GAA）製程雲端AI專案訂單，這對智原意義重大，是最先進的製程，也是第1個2奈米GAA製程專案，複雜度也最高。

王國雍表示，原本客戶計劃採用4奈米製程，基於延長產品生命週期考量，決定改採2奈米製程；這專案總金額達數千萬美元，預計2027年上半年將有第1筆收入入帳，後續依進度認列，是智原史上最大金額的專案。

王國雍說，智原具備設計以及統籌協調能力，是能夠搶下2奈米專案的關鍵，此案將採用三星的晶圓代工，另外還與聯電及記憶體廠等夥伴合作。

智原第3季受惠量產業務優於預期，加上矽智財（IP）業績創下歷史新高，整體第3季營收攀高至新台幣36.64億元，季增10.6%，為歷年同期新高。

受產品組合變化影響，低毛利的量產業務比重攀升，智原第3季毛利率42.5%，較第2季下滑2.7個百分點，營業利益2.14億元，季減20.8%，受惠業外轉投資評價利益挹注，智原第3季歸屬母公司淨利2.79億元，季增40.8%，每股純益1.07元。

展望未來，智原預期，第4季IP業績可望持續成長創高，NRE業務將顯著成長，量產業務可能下滑，整體第4季營收將較第3季持平，毛利率約45%。

王國雍表示，2027年營收將成長2位數，包括IP、NRE和量產3大產品線2027年營收可望同步成長。

news.Title: Rambus Inc (RMBS) (Q3 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: Record Revenue and EPS as DDR5 Demand ...
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Total Revenue: $218 million, up 22% year over year and 5% sequentially; record high. Product Revenue: $114 million, up 22% year over year and 15% sequentially; all-time quarterly record. Royalties Revenue: $77 million. Contract and Other Revenue: $27 million, up 35% year over year and 13% sequentially (primarily silicon IP). Non-GAAP Operating Costs: $116 million total, including cost of goods sold. Operating Expenses: $70 million, down sequentially on slightly lower R&D and SG&A. Interest and Other Income: $7 million. Non-GAAP Net Income: $91.7 million (16% non-GAAP tax rate). Non-GAAP EPS: $0.84, up 35% year over year and 10% sequentially. Cash, Cash Equivalents & Marketable Securities: $777 million, down $48 million from Q2. Cash Flow from Operations: Record $102 million. Share Repurchases: $135 million, including a $100 million accelerated share repurchase program. Inventory: Increased $12 million to support future product ramps. Q4 Revenue Guidance: $227 million$233 million. Q4 Product Revenue Guidance: $127 million$133 million (midpoint up 34% year over year, 14% sequentially). Q4 Royalties Guidance: $68 million$74 million. Q4 Contract and Other Guidance: $26 million$32 million. Q4 Non-GAAP Operating Costs Guidance: $120 million$124 million. Q4 Capital Expenditures Guidance: ~$8 million. Q4 Non-GAAP Operating Profit Guidance: $103 million$113 million. Q4 Non-GAAP EPS Guidance: $0.84$0.92 (midpoint up 30% year over year, 5% sequentially). Full-Year 2026 Outlook: Revenue growth ~18% over 2025; product revenue growth ~24%; non-GAAP EPS growth ~24%. Is RMBS fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Release Date: October 26, 2026 For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript . Positive Points Rambus Inc ( NASDAQ:RMBS ) achieved record revenue and non-GAAP earnings in Q3, exceeding the top end of guidance, with revenue of $218 million, up 22% year over year. Product revenue reached an all-time high of $114 million, up 15% sequentially and 22% year over year, driven by strong demand for DDR5 RCDs and new generation products. Rambus Inc ( NASDAQ:RMBS ) expects Q4 product revenue to grow more than 30% year over year, with total revenue guidance of $227-233 million, implying 18% annual growth for 2026. The company is expanding its product portfolio with new offerings like the sixth-generation RCD and industry-leading PMIC for LPDDR6 SOCAMM2, positioning it well for future server platforms. Silicon IP business is growing towards the higher end of the 10-15% range, with key design wins across HBM, PCIe, and security IP, reinforcing long-term growth opportunities. Story Continues Negative Points MRDIMM ramp is expected to be shallower than previous RCD generations due to staged platform adoption and memory despecing, which could limit near-term revenue contribution. Product gross margins were at the lower end of the 60-63% range in Q3, primarily due to supply chain input cost inflation, and may remain under pressure. Supply chain lead times are increasing, and while Rambus Inc ( NASDAQ:RMBS ) is mitigating with inventory build, tight supply could constrain future growth if demand accelerates further. The LPDDR6 PMIC and SOCAMM2 products are not expected to contribute significantly until 2028, representing a niche opportunity with a longer adoption timeline. Visibility into customer inventory levels is limited, making it difficult to assess potential double-ordering or inventory buildup in the supply chain, which could impact future demand forecasts. Q & A Highlights Q : Kevin Garrigan (Jefferies) asked what is driving the Q4 product revenue guidance of roughly 34% year-over-year growth, and how much comes from companion chips or initial MRDIMM shipments versus RCDs. A : CEO Luc Seraphin said the growth reflects both rising market demand and multiple products ramping, with new-generation RCDs making up the bulk. Companion chips, which were low-double-digit percentage of product revenue at the start of the year, continue to grow sequentially. MRDIMM remains very modest, with Qual and pre-production shipments this year and the AMD platform just starting to ramp. Q : Kevin Garrigan (Jefferies) asked what is different about the next-generation MRDIMM opportunity that gives Rambus confidence it can take a leadership position, given a competitor was designed into the first-generation platform. A : CEO Luc Seraphin said MRDIMM is tied to a single platform launch, so the ramp will be shallower than a standard RCD ramp because not all platforms ramp at once and customers must adopt a new technology. He also noted memory despecing, where module counts rise but per-module capacity falls. Rambus still sizes the MRDIMM opportunity at $600 million in total. Q : Gary Mobley (StoneX) asked how Rambus sees seasonality and visibility for the first half of 2027 given the strong second half and backlog. A : CEO Luc Seraphin said demand is strengthening into 2027 with better backlog visibility, and he is optimistic about the year. He expects some normal first-half versus second-half seasonality in 2027, but in aggregate is confident in the health of demand growth. Q : Gary Mobley (StoneX) asked whether the silicon IP business is trending above the roughly $130 million annual run rate, and whether Rambus can forge long-term development arrangements with hyperscalers building custom silicon. A : CFO Sumeet Gagneja said silicon IP is growing toward the higher end of the 10% to 15% range, with 2026 a strong year and good design win momentum. CEO Luc Seraphin said Rambus is engaging earlier with the ecosystem on complex chips, including PCIe 7, PCIe 7 switch, HBM4 and data center security IP, and sees potential to expand the portfolio organically or inorganically and partner with customers at the system level. Q : Sebastien Naji (William Blair) asked how the new LPDDR6 PMIC for SOCAMM2 increases dollar content per module versus the earlier SOCAMM2 chipset, and when initial revenue is expected. A : CEO Luc Seraphin declined to give exact content before the final spec is released, but said dollar content increases from the first to the second SOCAMM generation as power management becomes more complex and module performance improves. He said SOCAMM2 will likely reach the market around 2028 and addresses a niche but important part of AI infrastructure. Q : Sebastien Naji (William Blair) asked why Q3 non-GAAP product gross margin of about 60.4% was at the low end of the 60% to 63% near-term range, and how Q4 margins should trend. A : CFO Sumeet Gagneja said the lower end was primarily driven by supply chain input costs, offset by internal cost savings. He expects a slight uptick in Q4 but still within the 60% to 63% range, and said full-year 2026 should land in the middle of that range. The long-term target remains 60% to 65%. Q : Mark Lipacis (Evercore) asked about lead times from Rambus' own suppliers and to its customers, and whether downstream customers are building inventory. A : CEO Luc Seraphin said supply-side lead times are increasing, as anticipated, and Rambus is using its balance sheet to build inventory and work closely with suppliers. Q3 was not impacted and Q4 guidance is not expected to be impacted. Lead times to Rambus customers have not increased. He said customers are placing backlog earlier rather than visibly building inventory, though that is hard to determine. Q : Tristan Gerra (Baird) asked about confidence in meeting accelerating demand into 2027, whether product growth is sustainable, and whether supply will be an issue again next year. A : CEO Luc Seraphin said demand is strengthening into 2027 and supply will remain tight, but Rambus is working early and frequently with supply chain partners to secure capacity. He pointed to favorable CPU-to-GPU ratio trends supporting demand for Rambus products. Q : Tristan Gerra (Baird) asked about the medium-term content opportunity difference between x86 CPUs and standalone Arm-based CPUs, and whether SOCAMM cannibalizes standard DIMMs. A : CEO Luc Seraphin said Rambus views the market in aggregate and sees SOCAMM and LPDDR as complementary rather than cannibalizing standard DIMMs. Head nodes may use SOCAMM, but the majority of growth comes from standard servers and agentic CPUs with standard memory subsystems, which are expected to grow at a higher pace into 2027. Q : Kevin Cassidy (Rosenblatt) asked whether earlier involvement in custom chip design cycles helps Rambus win more module content as those designs reach production. A : CEO Luc Seraphin said silicon IP engagements with hyperscalers and custom silicon makers give Rambus insight into architectural trends, including where DIMMs versus LPDDR will be used and which DDR generations will be adopted. That helps Rambus shape its product roadmap and understand how customers will configure systems with different module types. Q : Kevin Cassidy (Rosenblatt) asked whether Rambus is comfortable with current inventory days or expects inventory to keep rising given increasing demand next year. A : CFO Sumeet Gagneja said Rambus grew inventory by $12 million in Q3 to provide greater supply assurance to customers, leveraging its balance sheet. He expects to increase inventory again in Q4 at a similar level to Q3 and Q2 given accelerating demand and better backlog visibility. news.Title: Bull of the Day: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM)
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM is one of, if not the most important companies in the world, making it a nearly surefire long-term investment in artificial intelligence and technology in general.

Taiwan Semi, or TSMC, physically manufactures the most cutting-edge semiconductors fueling the artificial intelligence boom and the wider tech-driven economy.

The chip builder reported a strong beat-and-raise Q3 on October 15, confirming that the AI capex spending spree remains full-steam ahead even as bubble concerns ramp up. The chart below showcases Taiwan Semi's impressive earnings expansion, including ~400% growth between 2019 and 2025.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

TSMC's Q4 earnings estimate surged ~12% since its mid-month release, while its FY27 estimate jumped significantly as well to help it earn a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Its robust guidance is supported by "continued strong demand" for its "leading-edge process technologies, including the steep ramp-up of our 2-nanometer technology."

The stock, which nearly quadrupled the Tech sector over the last 15 years and tripled it over the past five, is down ~12% from its recent peaks.

TSMC is on the verge of a possible technical breakout, and it is trading at a 43% discount to its highs and in line with its 10-year median at 19.5X forward earnings.

TSMC: Is This the Best Tech Stock to Buy Now and Hold Forever?

AI and the global economy rely, directly or indirectly, on semiconductors. More importantly, TSMC likely manufactured a large share of the chips fueling the AI boom and beyond, since the chip builder reportedly captures 60% of the foundry market and 90% of advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

The company on a tiny island doesn't design or sell its own semiconductors. Instead, TSMC was founded in the late 1980s on a simple, yet revolutionary "pure-play foundry" model, dedicated exclusively to manufacturing advanced semiconductors for other tech companies.

Taiwan Semi has built an almost unbreachable fortress around its leading-edge chip-building business by earning the trust of customers such as Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), AMD, Qualcomm, and other tech titans.

Nvidia, Apple, and others rely on TSMC because of its unmatched scale and expertise. Plus, their CEOs know that Taiwan Semi is their partner, not a competitor. The company is also critically rushing to expand its global manufacturing operation outside of Taiwan into the U.S., Japan, and beyond to address one of its only potential shortfalls: geopolitics.

Story Continues

What AI Bubble? Buy Taiwan Semi Stock for AI-Boosted Growth

Wall Street is still waiting for Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia, and many other tech firms to report third-quarter earnings. But TSMC already confirmed that the AI capital spending boom is ramping up.

TSM grew its Q3 earnings by 58% on 41% higher revenue. The chip builder said that 3- nanometer shipments accounted for 33% of its total wafer revenue, up from 23% in the year-ago period. Plus, its most advanced 2-nm chips accounted for 8%, up from 3% in the second quarter (first time 2-nm shipments were broken out in its earnings release).

TSMC's Q4 earnings estimate surged 12% since its Q3 release on October 15, with its fiscal 2027 estimate 6% higher. The recent positivity extends its impressive run of upward earnings revisions, and its most accurate estimates for FY26 and FY27 came in above consensus. The tech giant's overall upbeat earnings revisions land it a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) right now.

The leading chip builder said at the start of 2026 that it expects to grow its revenue by a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of ~25% between 2024 and 2029.

TSMC is projected to grow its revenue by 41% in 2026 and another 33% next year to reach $229 billion, adding more than $100 billion vs. 2025's $122 billion total and more than tripling its 2023 figure.

On the bottom line, it's projected to grow its earnings by 60% in 2026 and 32% next year, more than doubling its 2025 total ($10.65) in the process ($22.44 a share in 2027). TSMC's robust guidance is supported by "continued strong demand" for its "leading-edge process technologies, including the steep ramp-up of our 2-nanometer technology."

On top of that, Taiwan Semi has topped our quarterly earnings estimates for five years running.

Buy This Top-Ranked Tech Stock Now for Value and Breakout Potential?

Taiwan Semi stock soared ~3,300% in the last 15 years to blow away Tech's ~870%. More recently, TSM stock outclimbed the entire Mag 7 over the last year, up ~44%.

The chip builder is nearly neck-and-neck with Nvidia over the last three years, skyrocketing ~400%, while leaving the rest of the Mag 7 in the dust.

TSM is down roughly 12% from its October 5 records, and its average Zacks price target implies 27% upside from Monday's levels.

Some of its drop can be attributed to the laws of market gravity. The stock reached heavily overbought RSI levels to start October. TSM stock is attempting to retake its 50-day and its long-term 21-week moving averages.

The pullback, coupled with its strong earnings growth outlook, has TSMC trading at a 43% discount to its highs at 19.5X forward 12-month earnings.

The chip builder is also trading almost directly in line with the Tech sector, the S&P 500, and TSMC's 10-year median, even though it has climbed ~1,300% in the past decade vs. the Zacks Tech sector's ~470%.

On top of all that, TSMC's balance sheet is robust and supports its various expansion efforts. And 16 of the 19 brokerage recommendations that Zacks has are "Strong Buys."

Disclosure: Ben Rains owns TSM stock in his personal portfolio.

news.Title: 台股急殺失守46K！ 記憶體力挺撐盤 南亞科一度飆8%
news.Content:
台股今（27）日上演大怒神行情！受美股反彈激勵，加權指數早盤開高走高，一度大漲逾500點、衝上4萬6585點，不料隨後賣壓出籠，欣興（3037）、台光電（2383）等高價股翻黑，指數急轉直下，盤中上下震盪逾908點，再度失守4萬6千點。截至中午11時58分，加權指數暫報45924.94點，下跌116.49點，跌幅0.25%，成交金額已達6841億元。盤面上，記憶體族群成為資金焦點，南亞科（2408）、華邦電（2344）逆勢走強。

記憶體族群點火

記憶體族群今日表現亮眼，受到韓國半導體大廠股價反彈帶動，南亞科盤中最高衝上449元，漲幅達8.45%，截至上午11時58分暫報442元，上漲6.76%；華邦電上漲4.21%，報161元，旺宏（2337）上漲2.51%，力積電（6770）上漲4.67%。此外，晶豪科（3006）上漲5.77%，十銓（4967）上漲4.6%，記憶體模組及相關封測股也多數走揚。市場另有投顧報告預估，明年DDR4供需缺口可能達20%，為相關族群帶來想像空間。不過，南亞科近期仍面臨法人調節，投信已連續8個交易日賣超，累計賣超逾1.6萬張，後續買盤能否延續仍受關注。

高價股翻黑拖累大盤

台股早盤原本氣勢如虹，台積電、記憶體、ABF載板及AI概念股同步帶動指數上攻，但隨著欣興、台光電等高價股賣壓湧現，盤勢迅速翻轉，大盤由大漲轉為下跌，再度跌破4萬6千點。個股方面，記憶體相關股多數上漲，巨虹則逆勢下挫8.09%，暫報12.50元，成為盤面弱勢股之一。市場在急漲急跌間震盪，顯示資金追價態度仍有分歧。

旺宏、力成下午法說

今日盤面另一項觀察重點，是旺宏與力成（6239）將於下午舉行第三季法人說明會，公布最新財報及第四季營運展望。記憶體報價走勢、供需變化，以及相關封測需求能否延續，預料都將成為法人關注焦點。

（封面圖／東森新聞）

news.Title: Global chip, AI stocks surge on Anthropic IPO cheer
news.Content:
Investing.com-- Global chipmakers and AI-related stocks rallied on Tuesday after Anthropic filed for an initial public offering (IPO), reviving optimism about AI demand.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

U.S.-listed shares of SK Hynix rose 2.2% in early U.S. trading by 09:42 ET (13:42 GMT), while Micron climbed 2.3%, and Broadcom jumped 4.7%. AMD and Intel rose more than 3% each.

Neocloud stocks CoreWeave and Nebius surged 6% and 10.7%, respectively.

In Europe, ASM International rose 3.7%, and STMicroelectronics gained 4.4%. Germany's Infineon added 2.8%. BE Semiconductor surged more than 10%, though those gains primarily came after Applied Materials announced plans to raise its stake in Besi to 20% from 9%.

In Asia, South Korea's Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) shares closed 5.2% higher in Seoul trading, while SK Hynix Inc (KS:000660) climbed 4.2%.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Japanese semiconductor equipment makers Tokyo Electron (TYO:8035) rose 3.1%, and Advantest Corp. (TYO:6857) surged 9%.

Japan's top AI investor SoftBank Group (TYO:9984) shares also climbed 5%.

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, on Monday disclosed rapid revenue growth alongside steep losses in its IPO filing, highlighting both the commercial potential of generative AI and the substantial costs of developing advanced models.

Markets now await results from major U.S. technology companies this week for evidence that AI investment is translating into sustainable profits.

Vahid Karaahmetovic contributed to this report.

news.Title: Rambus (RMBS) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
news.Content:
Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Oct. 26, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

Chief Financial Officer - Sumeet Gagneja

President and Chief Executive Officer - Luc Seraphin

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator: Welcome to the Rambus Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Earnings Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Sumeet Gagneja, Chief Financial Officer. You may begin your conference.

Sumeet Gagneja: Thank you, operator, and welcome to Rambus Third Quarter 2026 Results Conference Call. I'm Sumeet Gagneja, Chief Financial Officer at Rambus. On the call with me today is Luc Seraphin, our CEO. The press release for the results that we will be discussing today has been filed with the SEC on Form 8-K. We are webcasting this call along with the slides that we will reference during portions of today's call. A replay of this call will be available on our website beginning today at 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time. Our discussion today will contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for projected financial results and prospects, market growth, demand for our solutions and the potential effects of geopolitical and macroeconomic conditions.

These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that may be discussed during this call and are more fully described in our documents we file with the SEC, including our 8-Ks, 10-Qs and 10-Ks. These forward-looking statements may differ materially from our actual results, and we are under no obligation to update these statements. In our press release and on the call today, we present both GAAP and non-GAAP financial measures to provide greater clarity regarding our financial performance. A reconciliation of these non-GAAP financials to the most directly comparable GAAP measures has been included in our press release, in our slide presentation and on our website at rambus.com on the Investor Relations page under Financial Releases.

The order of the call today will be as follows: Luc will begin with an overview of the business, followed by my review of the financial results, and then we'll open the call to Q&A. I will now turn the call over to Luc to provide an overview of the quarter. Luc?

Luc Seraphin: Thank you, Sumeet. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. In Q3, we delivered a truly exceptional quarter. Revenue and non-GAAP earnings both reached new record highs and exceeded the top end of our guidance ranges. Strong customer demand fueled record product revenue and cash from operations, and we expect an even stronger product performance in Q4. We introduced new chip and silicon IP products that extend our leadership in data center and AI infrastructure. In addition, as complexity and pace accelerate in semiconductor development for AI, we are also investing in the tools and infrastructure that will keep us on the leading edge of technology.

Story Continues

As such, we engaged with a fellow pioneer in the ecosystem and announced an exciting new partnership that propels us into the age of AI agent-driven chip and IP design. As we continue to invest in our future, we are also pleased to have completed a $100 million accelerated share repurchase. This demonstrates the strength of our business model and our ability to return value to our stockholders while advancing our product road map to drive long-term growth.

Taken together, the results and progress we delivered this quarter reflect the strength and long-term resilience of a strategy we have pursued over many years, investing in technology leadership, anticipating the key trends transforming the data center and positioning the company to capture the opportunities those trends create. Our strategy is producing strong results today, while at the same time, laying the foundation for future growth. As we outlined over previous quarters, AI continues to create strong tailwinds for Rambus across our businesses. As frontier AI training continues to advance and inference scales across a growing range of applications, customers require increasingly sophisticated memory and infrastructure architectures to move, manage and secure growing volumes of data.

Agentic AI is accelerating this trend as deployments evolve toward more distributed and heterogeneous architectures that require greater coordination across systems. At the same time, orchestration of always-on workloads puts greater demands on the CPU, lifting CPU to GPU ratios and driving requirements for more main memory bandwidth and capacity across the data center. The latest agentic implementations amplify this need even further by assigning dedicated compute and memory resources to individual users or agents.

All this creates accelerating demand for Rambus products and IP throughout the memory subsystem and across the broader infrastructure stack, while we continue to invest in the fundamental R&D and product road map required to address the ever-growing demand of memory management efficiency in the long run. Now let me turn to the quarterly results, starting with products. We delivered a new all-time high in quarterly product revenue, reaching approximately $114 million, up 15% sequentially and 22% year-over-year. Our leadership in DDR5 RCDs and growing adoption of new generation products fueled our record results.

We are seeing strong demand across multiple generations of RCDs, supporting our outlook for another record quarter of product revenue in Q4, which we expect to grow more than 30% year-over-year. Looking ahead, we have a strong pipeline of products aligned with upcoming platform ramps, positioning us well for next generation of server platforms. As part of that pipeline, we are pleased to share that our sixth-generation RCD announced early in Q3, which supports DDR5 9600, is now sampling broadly with customers and is being very well received. We continue to execute successfully on our road map, recently expanding our product portfolio with an industry-leading PMIC for the upcoming LPDDR6 SOCAMM2.

Earlier this year, we introduced our first SOCAMM2 chipset that supports LPDDR5X. This new PMIC solution extends our server memory product road map to LPDDR6 and reinforces our leadership in advanced server memory power management. It was developed in close collaboration with customers and ecosystem partners to enhance memory subsystem power efficiency and help scale tokens per watt for AI workloads. We identified early on that power management would be critical to the success of AI deployments and have been investing in this area for many years. We are proud of our progress and continued leadership in this space.

We have consistently said that as memory speeds increase and server architectures become more sophisticated and heterogeneous, the memory subsystem will require additional intelligence, power management and control functionality. Our road map is designed to address this evolution across both DDR and LPDDR-based memory with timing management, power management and security management, creating opportunities for Rambus to participate in increasing module chip content over time. In addition, DDR-based server platforms are expanding from 8 memory channels to 12 to 16 channels, increasing the maximum available memory bandwidth and capacity. This raises the number of modules supported in a server and amplifies demand as platforms progress.

Today, Rambus offers complete chipsets across all major industry standard DDR5 and LPDDR server memory module architectures. This broad portfolio positions us well for future server platforms and allows customers to leverage Rambus solutions across a growing range of memory architectures and deployment models. Looking ahead, we believe we are exceptionally well positioned for future server generations and for the continued expansion of memory-intensive AI infrastructure. Turning now to silicon IP. We delivered a very strong quarter with key design wins across our silicon IP portfolio.

The strength of those wins, combined with expanding strategic engagement across the industry, including custom silicon makers and hyperscalers, reinforces our confidence in the long-term growth opportunity for the silicon IP business and for Rambus. One of the defining characteristics of today's market is the rapid growth of custom silicon. The expansion of AI is fueling a new wave of custom silicon development. Hyperscalers, AI infrastructure providers and emerging semiconductor companies are designing increasingly differentiated architectures and tailored silicon optimized for their own environments. These systems depend on advanced memory technologies, high-speed interconnects and trusted security, creating significant opportunities for Rambus silicon IP.

During the quarter, we drove increasing ecosystem engagement and new Tier 1 design wins for next-generation HBM, supported by our deep architectural engagements ahead of standards being finalized. We continue to see increasing interest in PCIe controller and switch IP for scale-up and scale-out connectivity solutions as customers seek higher levels of performance and efficiency across rapidly expanding AI infrastructure. The importance of bleeding edge IP continues to increase as customers pursue differentiated performance, power efficiency and time-to-market advantages. As a result, we are engaging earlier in the architectural planning cycle with both our customers as well as our customers' customers and participating in a broader set of strategic programs. Leading edge memory and connectivity are fundamental to performance.

And as AI infrastructure scales and becomes more heterogeneous, hardware-based security foundation is becoming fundamental. Agentic AI relies on distributed computing architectures that execute workloads across multiple systems, which increases the available attack surface for adversaries, a growing concern in the current environment. As a pioneer and long-time leader in hardware-based security, Rambus IP solutions address that risk by providing a trusted foundation for the entire system and enhancing protection for valuable data and infrastructure. Building on our industry-leading security offerings, we recently added a new root of trust solution designed specifically for AI and data center deployments that supports the Caliptra specification.

Caliptra was developed by key leading technology companies to establish a common hardware security foundation for data center class SoCs and reflects the growing recognition that hardware-based security is essential for next-generation infrastructure. Looking across both chips and silicon IP, we will continue to drive solutions that address the long-term foundation memory performance, high-speed connectivity and robust security demands of AI infrastructure. At the same time, we are harnessing AI to advance the underlying tools and development infrastructure that enable us to move faster, extend our leadership and scale the business more effectively.

As I mentioned at the beginning of the call, we recently announced a strategic investment and collaboration with ChipAgents, a fellow industry pioneer and leader in agentic AI design platforms. We see great opportunities to leverage the ChipAgents AI native design flows to accelerate our road map by speeding the pace of our chip and IP development, improving design quality and enhancing engineering productivity across our organization. We believe this collaboration further strengthens our competitive position, both for products and for IP and reinforces Rambus's leadership role in next generation of AI data center infrastructure.

In summary, the company delivered an exceptional third quarter, and we expect an even stronger Q4 as we continue to capitalize on the growing demand from AI. We achieved record revenue and earnings while expanding our chip and IP offerings. And at the same time, we are investing in our development infrastructure to address the growing opportunities ahead. These results and decisions reflect the strength of our strategy and the continued alignment between Rambus technology and the most important trends shaping AI and data center infrastructure. We are executing well and more importantly, we are continuing to invest for the future and build on a strong foundation of technology leadership and customer partnerships.

We are confident in our trajectory, our road map and our ability to drive continued profitable growth in 2027 and beyond. As always, I want to thank our customers, partners and employees for their continued trust and support. And with that, I'll turn the call over to Sumeet. Sumeet?

Sumeet Gagneja: Thank you, Luc, and good afternoon, everyone. We delivered an outstanding third quarter, achieving record revenue and earnings and record cash flow from operations. These results reflect the strength of our business model, growing demand for our products and technologies and disciplined execution across the company. Consistent with our balanced capital allocation strategy, we completed a $100 million accelerated share repurchase program during the quarter. The transaction demonstrates our confidence in the business and our commitment to returning capital to shareholders while preserving the flexibility to invest in the growth.

Looking ahead, we believe Rambus is well positioned to capitalize on the secular growth in AI infrastructure, data centers and advanced computing through the strength of our product and technology portfolio. With that, let me review our third quarter financial results. Third quarter revenue was $218 million, driven by strong product and contract revenue. This represents growth of 22% year-over-year and 5% sequentially. Product revenue was $114 million, which is up 22% year-over-year and up 15% sequentially. Royalties revenue was $77 million. Contract and other revenue was $27 million, up 35% year-over-year and 13% sequentially. Contract and other revenue consist primarily of silicon IP.

As a reminder, only a portion of our silicon IP revenue is reflected in contracts and other revenue, and the remaining portion is reported in royalties revenue. Total non-GAAP operating costs, including cost of goods sold for the quarter, were $116 million. Operating expenses were $70 million, down sequentially due to slightly lower R&D and SG&A expenses. Interest and other income for the quarter was $7 million. Using non-GAAP tax rate at 16%, non-GAAP net income for the quarter was $91.7 million, resulting in Q3 non-GAAP earnings per share of $0.84, which is up 35% year-over-year and up 10% sequentially. Now let me turn to the balance sheet details.

We ended the third quarter with cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $777 million, down $48 million from Q2. Record cash flow from operations of $102 million were offset by $135 million of share repurchases, including the $100 million accelerated share repurchase program. Capital allocation remains a key priority for us. We intend to continue investing in the business while returning 40% to 50% of free cash flows to shareholders over time, supported by our strong balance sheet and continued cash generation. Our capital allocation approach reflects our focus on driving shareholder value while investing in our growth and pursue long-term opportunities ahead.

We also leveraged the strength of our balance sheet to increase inventory by $12 million during the quarter, positioning us to support future product ramps and provide customers with greater supply assurance. Now let me turn to our non-GAAP outlook for the fourth quarter. As a reminder, the forward-looking guidance reflects our best estimates at this time, and our actual results could differ materially from what I'm about to review. We expect fourth quarter revenue to be between $227 million and $233 million. Product revenue is expected to be between $127 million and $133 million. At the midpoint of the guidance, it is an increase of 34% year-over-year and an increase of 14% sequentially.

Royalties revenue is expected to be between $68 million and $74 million and contract and other revenue is expected to be between $26 million and $32 million. We expect Q4 non-GAAP total operating costs, which include cost of sales, to be between $124 million and $120 million. We expect Q4 capital expenditures to be approximately $8 million. Non-GAAP operating profit for the fourth quarter is expected to be between a profit of $103 million and $113 million. We expect fourth quarter interest and other income to be approximately $6.5 million. Assuming a non-GAAP tax rate of 16% and 109 million diluted shares outstanding, we expect fourth quarter non-GAAP earnings per share to be in the range from $0.84 to $0.92.

At the midpoint of the guidance, this represents growth of 30% year-over-year and 5% sequentially. Overall, we are very pleased with our third quarter performance. Our record revenue, earnings and cash flow from operations demonstrate the breadth of our product and technology portfolio, the diversity of our revenue streams and the disciplined execution of our teams. The midpoint of our fourth quarter guidance implies that 2026 revenue will grow approximately 18% over 2025, including product revenue growth of approximately 24%. With our continued focus on driving growth and operating efficiency, we expect non-GAAP earnings per share to grow approximately 24% over 2025.

We remain focused on executing our strategy and capturing the opportunities created by AI infrastructure, data center and advanced computing markets. We are committed to translating these opportunities into sustainable growth, strong cash generation and long-term shareholder value. With that, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A. Operator, could we have our first question, please?

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Your first question comes from the line of Kevin Garrigan with Jefferies.

Kevin Garrigan: Congrats on the results. Luc, so Q3 product revenue growth was 22% year-over-year. The Q4 midpoint implies about 34%. And I know you talked about strong growth across RCD generations, but can you give us a sense of how much growth is coming from other areas like companion chip ramps or any initial MRDIMM shipments?

Luc Seraphin: Thanks, Kevin. Yes, we were really pleased with the results for Q3 and the growth for Q4, 34% year-over-year. We always saw that the second half of the year would be stronger than the first half of the year. I would say it's a combination of market demand going up and a lot of our products actually ramping into the market. The new generation of RCDs make the bulk of that. At the beginning of the year, we said that our companion chips were approximately low double-digit percentage of our product revenue and that it would grow sequentially quarter-over-quarter. We see this happening. MRDIMM remains very modest, actually. We have shipped MRDIMM for Qual and preproduction this year.

The AMD platform is starting to ramp. So it's still very modest. So we're really, really pleased with this 34% year-over-year growth based on the core, I would say, RCD and companion chips.

Kevin Garrigan: Okay. Great. And then as a follow-up, just on the MRDIMM opportunity. So the RCD playbook was always about being first to market and qualifying early. One of your competitors was designed for the first-generation MRDIMM platform. So what's different about this next generation that gives you confidence that you can take a leadership position?

Luc Seraphin: The difference with MRDIMM is that it's associated with the launch of a platform that is very different than what we have all seen for the past few years. There's only one platform that is supporting MRDIMM now growing into the market. We don't know what the production of MRDIMM is going to be compared to the standard DIMM in that area. So it's going to be a ramp, and we're confident this ramp will happen. We still believe this is a great opportunity for us that we still size at $600 million in total.

But the ramp will be shallower, in our opinion, than the other generations of products simply because all of the platforms are not ramping at the same time. This is a new technology, and our customers have to adopt this technology and go through the initial stumbles. There's also this thing that we see in the market of memory de-specing. It's not that people decrease the number of modules, but they tend to decrease the capacity of each one of these modules. So we do see a growth of the number of modules in the market that explains our growth in Q4.

But we do see at the same time that each one of these modules tend to have lower capacity and it's due to the economics of the memory at this point in time. So between the memory economics, the stage ramp of the platforms and the introduction of new technology and supply associated with that, we see this as a great opportunity, but we see the ramp to be shallower than the standard ramp of an RCD product.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Gary Mobley with StoneX.

Gary Mobley: Congrats on strong execution as we navigate through the second half of the year. Clearly, the second half of the year is playing out with seasonal strength on the product side as you had been communicating throughout the year. Based on what seems to be strong market environment and your existing backlog, how would you call out the seasonality of the first half of the year? Were you seeing something a little atypical, maybe slightly better than seasonal in the first half of the year? How do you see your visibility playing into the first half of the year on the product side?

Luc Seraphin: Yes. So you're correct, Gary. The second half of the year, we have this seasonal effect that is advantageous to us. I would add to this for this year that I think we're really pleased with the execution. We do see our companion chip ramp in earnest, for example, a new generation being adopted at a higher rate than they used to be. When we look into 2027, I would say that we see demand strengthening. I think this is not going down. So we're quite optimistic for 2027. The demand is strengthening. We have a better visibility into our backlog going into 2027.

I think we're going to continue to see some sort of seasonality between the first half and the second half in 2027. But in aggregate, we are confident with the health of the demand growth in 2027.

Gary Mobley: As my follow-up, I wanted to ask about the silicon IP business. I think you've been communicating that this might be a $130 million annual business. I would assume that you're maybe trending above that. Can you confirm or give us any color on that? And then with respect to custom ASIC development, do you see an opportunity, whether it be on high-speed SerDes interface IP, high-speed memory interface IP or security IP to forge a long-term development arrangement with some of the hyperscalers developing custom silicon, like what we've seen with some of the other competitors in the IP space?

Luc Seraphin: Yes. So Gary, I'll start with the second question about the potential for silicon IP, and then I'll ask Sumeet to answer on the revenue and the revenue growth. We are engaging more and more with the ecosystem on the silicon IP because people are building more and more complex chips that require more and more complex integration and on the bleeding edge of technology. This is, for example, what we described in our last call with the engagement with a hyperscaler on next generation of memory. So we see our confidence in the silicon IP keeps increasing. If you look at our product rollout, we talk about PCIe 7.0, IP PCIe 7.0 switch.

HBM4, next generations of HBM, these dedicated security solutions for the data center. So we are engaged deeply with the ecosystem that gives us the opportunity going forward to potentially continue to increase our portfolio, not only organically but possibly inorganically and also to partner with our customers to develop broader system. So as part of our thinking for silicon IP, we have that notion of working more and more with our partners on the system level. By the way, the announcement we made about agentic AI helps us do that. The ability to have agents work with us on integrating IP in much more complex systems is actually enabled by this type of things.

So we're building the infrastructure to do that, that's the direction we are going into. It's going to take us time, but that is definitely a great trend for us. I'll let Sumeet answer on the numbers, yes.

Sumeet Gagneja: Yes. Thanks, Luc. And just to add to that, Gary. So yes, so we've said our silicon IP business around $130 million, growing at 10% to 15%. But like Luc said, our confidence has been building throughout the year and 2026 has been a great year for our silicon IP business, along with the strong momentum in the design wins. So I would put it more like we're growing more towards the higher end of that range. We've said 10% to 15%, and we continue to make progress in all aspects from memory interface and security aspects.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Sebastien Naji with William Blair.

Sebastien Cyrus Naji: Maybe first, I wanted to ask about the LPDDR6 PMIC that you announced. Could you maybe give us a sense for how that increases your dollar content per module versus the SOCAMM2 content that you had announced in April? I think it was 2 voltage regulators and an SPD hub. And then when do you expect maybe some initial revenue for that product?

Luc Seraphin: Thanks, Sebastien. I would say that I'll be a bit discreet about the exact content on this SOCAMM2 because it's not -- the final spec has not been released yet. So I'd rather wait for the final spec to be released. But what I can say is that when you move from the first version of SOCAMM that we announced earlier this year to this new generation of SOCAMM2, the content is increasing. The power management is more complex. And as a result of that, the dollar content is going to increase from that first generation to that second generation.

The module performance itself is going to be much better as well, which will, I would say, trigger adoption at a higher level. But as every one of these SOCAMM solutions, they provide a very good solution for these areas of AI where power performance is really, really important. But this is a small portion of the market, and that's going to be continuing -- that's continued to be the case between the first version of SOCAMM2 and the SOCAMM2. The SOCAMM2 will hit the market probably in 2028. And the way to look at it is we see the development of the AI infrastructure as having multiple horizons for us, if you wish.

We want to make sure that we develop those solutions way ahead of the market. And when they deploy in the market, then we are present with solutions that work. This is what we've done in the past that explains, for example, our performance in Q4 this year that are based a lot on the products we developed in the past. They had little traction at the beginning, but they're starting to show revenues in Q4 of this year. This is going to be the same with SOCAMM. SOCAMM is going to address a niche portion of the AI stack, AI infrastructure. But the adoption of LP is going to happen. It's not going to happen fast.

It's not going to be the same content as the current content of standard memory. But it's important for us to have that as part of our portfolio while we help our customers and ecosystem partners to deploy their solutions in the market.

Sebastien Cyrus Naji: Great. Okay. That's very helpful. And then maybe my second question or my follow-up for Sumeet on gross margins. It looks like non-GAAP product gross margins were about 60.4% in Q3. That's on the lower end of the, I think, 60% to 63% near-term range that you gave us. Could you maybe give us a sense for how much of the gap here is mix in terms of just more companion chip revenue, next-generation RCDs with early yields versus how much of it is wafer substrate or OSAT cost inflation? And then how should we think about Q4 product gross margins? Do they stay in that lower 60% area? Or can they move up a little bit?

Sumeet Gagneja: Yes. Thanks for the question, Sebastien. Yes. So our gross margin historically has been this tight band, 60% to 63%. And you're right, in the Q3 was slightly above 60%. Our long-term target remains, which is 60% to 65%. In the near term, it's really the margin trending towards the lower end is primarily driven by the supply chain input cost. And we've been very successful in offsetting that cost input cost by driving internal cost savings and keeping our product gross margin in the range of 60% to 63% in the near term.

Q4, it's the same sort of the setup going into Q4, but the investments and the cost reductions we have done especially in our operations side, there may be a slight uptick in the gross margin in Q4, but it's not material, but it's still within the 60% to 63%. On a full year basis, it's more important to look at from the gross margin perspective. We expect 2026 to be right in the middle of that 60% to 63% range.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Mark Lipacis with Evercore.

Mark Lipacis: I had 2. I was hoping you could just talk about lead times from your own suppliers and any -- to the extent that you're seeing tightening supply on the front end or the back-end foundry business? And then can you talk about lead times to your customers? And are there any stretching of lead times to your customers from you? And any indication that your customers downstream or the supply chain downstream is increasing their own inventories given how tight everything seems to be becoming?

Luc Seraphin: Thanks, Mark. I'll start and let Sumeet comment. I would say that on the supply side, we do see lead times increasing. We signaled this 2 calls ago. We were expecting this. But because we were expecting this, we also put in place plans to mitigate for that. So we lever our strong balance sheet to actually build inventory on products that we believe are going to grow substantially with our customers, and we're in constant relationship with our suppliers to make sure that we use our balance sheet to make sure that we can supply to our customers.

So yes, definitely longer lead times on the supply side, but it has not impacted our Q3 number, and it will not impact the Q4 number that we just talked about. So we've been able to manage that, but we have to continue to do that. Our lead times, the first approximation, our lead times to our customers have not increased at this point in time. But you understand that we are in constant discussions with them as well. The whole chain is tightening. The good thing is our business is very focused. We have very strong partnerships with our customers, and we work with them in making sure that we can supply what they need.

In summary, longer lead times on the supply side, we are using our balance sheet to deal with that. And at this point in time, we've not increased our lead times to our customers.

Mark Lipacis: And just to be clear, do you have the ability to see if customers or customers' customers downstream are increasing their inventories? Or is that like a black box to you and it's really hard to determine?

Luc Seraphin: It's very hard to determine. We see -- what we see is that people place backlog earlier than what they used to a quarter ago or 2 quarters ago. I think everyone understands the current situation. So we have better visibility in the backlog. But at the same time, that gives us more opportunity to have a deeper, I would say, relationship with our customers. Once we understand the profile of their backlog, then it's easier to work with them on how we can lead that backlog. So we don't see people building inventory, but we see people placing backlog.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Tristan Gerra with Baird.

Tristan Gerra: So if I heard well, you mentioned that your revenue in the quarter and the guidance is not constrained by supply. So it probably provides a little bit of an easy comp relative to the first half where you did face some supply issues. What's your level of confidence that you can actually meet the accelerating demand that you described into next year? And I know you're not guiding beyond this quarter, but do you think that the acceleration that you're seeing in product revenue year-over-year is sustainable? Or do you see supply as an issue again next year?

And is there any talk about longer-term agreements or anything that customers are trying to set up to ensure supply from here?

Luc Seraphin: So we see demand -- thank you, Tristan. We see demand strengthening into next year, and we started to work with our supply chain partners to meet what we believe is going to be required. In all honesty, this is something that we work on almost on a weekly basis. We try all avenues to support our customer base. So demand is strong going into 2027. Supply will remain tight. But as I said, as we did in 2026, we're working early with our supply base to look at every knob we can turn to support our customer demand. That's how we look at this.

The good news is that the demand for the products we have in our portfolio is strong. The demand for CPUs, this CPU to GPU ratio is going in our favor. It's known from our customers all the way down to our suppliers, and we'll do our best to supply that growing demand into 2027.

Tristan Gerra: Great. And then as a quick follow-up, I wanted to explore the difference in content opportunity medium term for x86 CPU and stand-alone Vera and kind of come up with maybe a 4x content in x86 CPU for you versus what you would get on the SOCAMM2 side with -- but are you quantifying at all what the opportunity is and the difference that you see in terms of opportunities on the x86 and the Arm-based side of CPUs next year and the years beyond?

Luc Seraphin: Yes. Thank you, Tristan. The way we look at it and the reason we are excited about this AI infrastructure deployment is that we look at this in an aggregate way. There are areas of AI like if you take the head nodes, for example, where SOCAMM and LP memory can be used. It's not always used, but it can be used. And that's an opportunity for us from a technology standpoint. It allows us to develop our LP technology on all fronts. But in aggregate, you do have a growth in these head nodes that will create an opportunity for SOCAMM.

But you have higher growth in the traditional servers with a refresh necessary in order to continue to develop the range of applications, or range of standard applications, we have higher growth in agentic, standard CPUs as well for orchestration, tools management, memory management. So in aggregate, if you take the head nodes where you can have SOCAMM and if you take the standard servers and the agentic server, the whole market is growing. But the majority of the growth is coming from CPUs with standard memory subsystems. So that's the way we look at it. We definitely don't look at this as SOCAMM is cannibalizing the market for standard DIMM. It's actually complementary. It makes the system more efficient.

The standard memory subsystems are going to increase at a higher pace going into 2027. And the head nodes will drive new technologies like SOCAMM to maximize this kind of application. So we see this as complementary, and that's why we want to have solutions for all of that. We really want to be agnostic to the memory subsystems while the infrastructure for AI is growing in the market because as that infrastructure is growing in the market, we're going to see heterogeneous systems, and it's important that we have solutions for each one of those. But the vast majority is going to continue to be CPU with standard DIMM configurations.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Kevin Cassidy with Rosenblatt Securities.

Kevin Cassidy: I'll echo the congratulations on a great quarter. Just -- it's interesting, as you mentioned about the custom chips and that you're getting involved earlier into the design cycle. And I'm just wondering if -- any way, does this help you to win more modules on those designs as they come into production?

Luc Seraphin: Thanks, Kevin. We're really excited with these silicon IP engagements with the ecosystem because they give us great insight into the architectural trends that these people are talking about. When we talk to hyperscalers with the opportunity for us to sell our silicon IP, we have insights into some of the architecture problems they're trying to resolve and where they see the world going. And as a consequence of that, that helps us develop -- continue to develop the right road map of products for these types of products.

But it also gives us insight as to the overall architecture of their systems and where DIMM are going to be used, where LP is going to be used and why, what generation of DDR is going to be used and why. It just gives us that channel of information. It's almost through the discussion, and it gives us a good sense of the trends in terms of what type of technologies they are going to use, not only on the silicon IP side, but also in terms of how they will configure their systems with different types of modules.

Kevin Cassidy: Right. And it seems like a big advantage over your 2 competitors that don't have IP story. And maybe just on the inventory one more time. Are you comfortable with the days of inventory now? Or should we expect to see that continue to increase even with the increasing demand next year?

Sumeet Gagneja: Yes, Kevin, good question. So inventory, as you mentioned, we've been growing inventory this year. In Q3, we grew it again $12 million, again, primarily leveraging the strength of our balance sheet to make sure we provide greater assurance to our customers. In Q4 as well, looking at just like Luc mentioned throughout the call, like we have more visibility into the backlog. And as demand is accelerating, we do plan to build or increase inventory even in Q4, similar level to like we built in Q3 and Q2.

Operator: At this time, there are no further questions. This concludes the question-and-answer session. I would like to turn the conference back over to the company for closing remarks.

Luc Seraphin: Thank you to everyone who has joined us today for your continued interest and support. We look forward to speaking with you again soon. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. This concludes today's conference. You may now disconnect.

news.Title: Rambus Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Rambus, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Record third-quarter results: Revenue rose 22% year over year to $218 million, while non-GAAP EPS increased 35% to $0.84 and operating cash flow reached a record $102 million. Product revenue was boosted by strong demand for DDR5 registered clock drivers and newer memory-interface products.

Growth outlook remains strong: Rambus expects fourth-quarter revenue of $227 million to $233 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.84 to $0.92. Management said the outlook implies approximately 18% revenue growth and 24% product-revenue growth in 2026.

AI infrastructure is driving demand: The company cited expanding needs for memory bandwidth, HBM, PCIe connectivity and security products, while advancing its DDR5 9600 and LPDDR6 roadmaps. Rambus also repurchased $135 million of stock during the quarter and plans to return 40% to 50% of free cash flow to shareholders over time.

Rambus: Another AI Phoenix Ready to Rise From the Ashes of Correction

Rambus (NASDAQ:RMBS) reported record third-quarter revenue, non-GAAP earnings and operating cash flow, as demand for its memory-interface products and intellectual property continued to benefit from AI infrastructure investment.

Third-quarter revenue rose 22% year over year and 5% sequentially to $218 million. Product revenue reached a record $114 million, increasing 22% from a year earlier and 15% from the prior quarter. The company said its DDR5 registered clock driver, or RCD, products and adoption of newer-generation offerings supported the performance.
